Charonadaemons serve Charon (q.v.), boatman of the Lower Planes, and like him pilot small skiffs along the Styx. These thin, gray, pale-eyed humanoids are easier to summon than their master but more cunning and spiteful.

  • Summoning: normally found only on the Styx; they can be called by any of the conjuration/summoning spells in the PHB.
  • Fare: per passenger, a magic item, a bag of 10 platinum coins, or 2 gems of 50+ gp value. If not paid, it keeps everyone out of its boat and teleports itself and its craft away.
  • Travel: it can pilot its craft through the Astral and Ethereal Planes as well as the Lower Planes, and is sometimes sent to the Prime Material Plane to fetch someone at the bidding of Charon, the oinodaemon, or another powerful evil being.
  • Betrayal: even when paid (as opposed to sent by a higher evil force), there is a 15% chance it betrays its passengers: by taking them to the wrong place or plane (85%), or leading them into an ambush of charonadaemons and hydrodaemons (15%). Extra contributions to its hoard lower the chance.
  • Glowing eyes: when angered, its eyes glow fiery red; anyone facing them must save vs. fear or flee in terror (as the spell).
  • Help: it can summon 1-6 hydrodaemons from the Styx to fight for it.
  • Telepathy: it speaks all languages and is always in contact with others of its race. Anyone who harms a charonadaemon gets no answer to his summons until he has made a suitable sacrifice and repentance: rare stones, magic, and a good intelligent being, offered in a desecrated temple of good.

Derghodaemons are natives of Hades, but are also found in Tartarus and Gehenna. Their round bodies have 5 arms and 3 legs, and their insect-like heads can turn all the way around, so they can move and change direction at will. They are extremely strong (as a stone giant) but also extremely stupid.

  • Claws: its 5 arms end in stubby, 4-clawed hands doing 1-4 points of damage, +8 for its strength.
  • Weapons: usually (60%) unarmed, but sometimes carries 1, 2, or 3 weapons (25%, 10%, and 5% respectively), each with a 20% chance of being magical. It attacks with claws first, then weapons.
  • Grabbing: if its first 2 claw attacks hit, it has grabbed the target, and its remaining claws or weapons attack at +2. A grabbed character can attack but cannot move or retreat until the derghodaemon is defeated. Against several attackers, the grab applies only to its first 2 attacks.
  • Parrying: if armed, it can parry, making its armor class −8 that round against 1 attacker.
  • Powers at will: darkness within 10 feet, fear (as a wand) within 20 feet, and teleport without error; sleep twice a day.
  • Summoning: stupid as they are, they are stubborn and hard to summon and control.
  • Treasure: type G in the lair. It also has a gizzard full of gems and other stones to help digestion, holding 0-3 gems of base 100 gp value.

These grotesque amphibians are the only creatures known to swim in the Styx without losing their memories, so they may be found in numbers (10-30) wherever the Styx and its branches run in the Lower Planes. They are often sent to serve evil on the Prime Material Plane. They prefer water, fire, or lava around them but can be found almost anywhere.

  • Gliding: they can launch into the air and glide like flying fish at high speed for up to 1 turn, sometimes using dimension door to gain height for a glide.
  • Attacks: airborne, 5 attacks: feet (1-4 each), hands (1-8 each), and bite (1-10); on the ground, 3 attacks. The bite also drains 1 life energy level.
  • Powers at will: teleport without error, darkness within 10 feet, create water, and water walking (as the ring).
  • Gate: another hydrodaemon, with a 50% chance of success.
  • Summon: on the Prime Material Plane, a 12 hit dice water elemental, which fights for it without needing control.
  • Water: besides normal daemon resistances, water-based attacks do half damage, or none if it makes its saving throw.

There is only one daemon master and lord of the Middle Planes, a unique being of great power known by the title oinodaemon. The present oinodaemon is Anthraxus the Decayed, to whom all daemons (in theory) pay homage. He is the most powerful daemon in the Lower Planes, but others challenge his position, chief among them Bubonis, Cholerix, Typhus, and Diptherius, with others unknown or unrecorded by scholars.

  • Touch: causes disease in life not from the Outer Planes; the disease prevents healing and is fatal in 1 week.
  • Gaze: can transfix 1 target per round, which cannot move until he allows it (a save vs. spell negates).
  • At will (once per melee round): pyrotechnics, flaming sphere, burning hands, shape change, detect magic, dispel magic, dispel illusion, delude, ESP, water breathing, teleport without error, and gate in 1-3 other daemons of his choice (85% chance of success).
  • Once per day: wall of fire, wall of ice, wall of force, minor globe of invulnerability, feeblemind, or cancellation as the rod.
  • He uses these abilities as a 25th-level magic-user.
  • The Staff of the Lower Planes: borne by the oinodaemon, and usable by another daemon only after Anthraxus dies. It has the powers of mass charm, beguilement (as the rod), geas, and granting another’s wish, which he uses only if it somehow leads to havoc and benefits evil. Its charm and beguilement work even on other daemons, automatically overcoming their magic resistance.
  • Psionics: body equilibrium, detection of good/evil, expansion, domination, sensitivity to psychic impressions, and the major sciences mind bar and molecular rearrangement (which he uses to turn lead into platinum), all at 20th level of mastery.

Description: a tall man in a rotting gray suit and cape, with the head of a disease-deformed ram. His mouth foams and the wool pulls away from the skin in handfuls. Boils and blisters cover his exposed skin, and his flesh is stretched tight over his bones.

The fish-tailed, wall-eyed piscodaemon has the red, chitinous body of a lobster, a bird’s talons, and the head of a carrion crawler. Its human-like arms end in crab-like pincers. It is found throughout the Lower Planes, usually serving more powerful daemons while bullying and tormenting anything weaker.

  • Seizing: it is quite strong. If both massive claws hit, it has seized the creature and draws it toward its mouth, then attacks with its short tentacles, trying to inject a venom fatal in 6 rounds (a save vs. poison means the character is only slowed for 6 rounds). Seized characters attack at −1 to hit. Poisoned characters may be carried off to be eaten later.
  • Eyes: its faceted eyes bulge from the sides of its head, letting it see around and behind, so it cannot be surprised.
  • Water: being aquatic, water-based attacks do −1 per damage die to it.
  • Service: piscodaemons are often summoned to the Prime Material Plane as laborers or guards. They resent such work and plot to overthrow and enslave their masters.

Shadowy ultrodaemons roam the Lower Planes at will, and few creatures dispute their power. They look like faceless humanoids with large eyes like fire opals.

  • Gaze: any being facing it must save vs. spells or stand fascinated (as from a hold person spell), watching the shifting colors and patterns. Those who save see not the ultrodaemon but someone they love or respect.
  • At will (once per round): fear by touch, charm person or charm monster, teleport without error, ESP, clairvoyance, clairaudience, illusion (as a wand), suggestion, mislead, magic jar, and telekinesis of 6,000 gp weight.
  • Once per day: wall of fire; a symbol of persuasion, insanity, or hopelessness; or blade barrier.
  • All these work as if cast by a 15th-level spell-caster.
  • Summoners: some ultrodaemons are said to have mastered summoning, and can call creatures from other planes, including the Prime Material Plane.

The yagnodaemon is a horrible creature with 2 unequal arms, one man-sized and the other giant-sized. With its giant’s arm it does damage as a storm giant (+12), unarmed or with its weapon, the tol-kendar.

The tol-kendar (“body-wrecker”): a huge 15-foot steel polearm topped by an upside-down cone ringed with blades and tipped with a harpoon-like point. Wielding it well takes a storm giant’s strength, and it is a wicked weapon in this daemon’s hands. It makes only 1 of these 2 attacks per round:

  • Tip: 1-10 points of damage (+ strength bonus) on a hit, and 1-6 the next round as it is pulled out.
  • Bladed sides: 1-8 (+ strength bonus), and 2-16 when pulled out.
  • Haft: any roll of 20 means it struck with the haft and knocked the opponent out for 2-12 rounds unless a save vs. paralysis is made.
  • Feeding: on a knocked-out opponent it feeds on the life force by pressing its head against the victim’s flesh, devouring 10-100% of the victim’s abilities before it is sated: experience points, hit points, psionic ability, and ability scores (strength, intelligence, etc.), fractions rounded up. This takes 5 melee rounds and can be interrupted if the victim wakes. Lost abilities return only through a restoration spell, or by killing the daemon within a day.
  • Other powers: teleport at will, and shocking grasp three times a day for 1-8 points +13, which it can deliver through its tol-kendar for extra damage.
  • Sturdy: earth-based attacks do half damage.

The dao come from the Elemental Plane of Earth and are related to the efreeti, djinni, jann, and marids (q.v.). They are uncommon even on their own plane, but love coming to the Prime Material Plane to work evil. They can travel the Prime Material, Elemental, and Astral Planes.

  • Spell-like powers (one at a time, once each per day): change self, detect good, detect magic, gaseous form, invisibility, granting another’s limited wish (in a perverse way), misdirection, passwall, spectral force, wall of stone. Also rock to mud 3 times per day and dig up to 6 times per day. They perform at 18th level of spell use.
  • Carrying: up to 5,000 gp weight without tiring. Double that weight tires them in 3 turns, but each 1,000 gp under 10,000 adds 1 turn; 6,000 gp, for example, allows 8 turns of walking or flying. After tiring they must rest 6 turns.
  • Earth travel: they move through earth (not worked stone) as if burrowing at 6”, but cannot take living beings with them.
  • Defenses: spells based on or affecting earth do not harm them. Holy water has double its normal effect on them.

Relations: only the efreet are friendly toward dao; dao hate djinn, jann, and marids. They dislike servitude as much as efreet do and are even more prone to malice and revenge.

Homes: the Great Dismal Delve on their own plane, and deep caves, caverns, or cysts on the Prime Material Plane. Their ruler is said to be a khan served by hetmen and atamen.

Languages: all the languages of geniekind, Common, and the languages of earth elementals.

This man-shaped monster lives only in bogs and similar marshy places where chill and damp prevail. It is pale and vaporous, well able to hide in the mists and fogs there.

  • Defenses: being largely insubstantial, it is normally armor class 0 and hit only by +2 or better magic weapons. Right after feeding it takes on substance: armor class 4, harmed by +1 or better magic weapons, and slower, for 6 turns.
  • Feeding: it surrounds its victim with vaporous tentacles and drains all the body fluids, then flushes crimson, which gives it its name.
  • Surprise: until it has fed it is nearly undetectable, surprising prey on 1-5 on d6.
  • Hiding the remains: it drags its victims’ remains to a bottomless bog or to its den, usually a thicket, a hollow under a windfall, or an undercut bank. In the den it keeps valuables from its victims to use later as bribes or lures for new ones.

system.description:
“Demilich” is a misleading name: the “demi” refers not to status but to the state of the lich. Only a small part of the body remains: dust, the skull, and perhaps a few bones. A lich (q.v.) is a human magic-user and/or cleric of surpassing evil who took steps to preserve its life force after death. In time even a lich’s undead life force wanes; over centuries the lich form decays, and the evil soul roams strange planes unknown to even the wisest sages. This remaining soul is the demilich.

The dust: when its resting place is entered, the dust swirls up into a man-like shape.

  • Ignored, it might fade in 3 rounds, since it sometimes (25%) can only advance and threaten, not harm. Usually (75%) it has the powers of a wraith even without extra energy factors.
  • Any physical attack on it gives it 1 energy factor, and spell attacks give 1 factor per spell level (a 3rd-level spell gives 3). Each factor equals a hit point. The dust wavers and falls back when struck by blow or spell, as if really hurt.
  • At 50 energy factors it forms a ghost manifestation controlled by the demilich, which attacks at once. So a ghost manifestation is quite likely even if there was no wraith manifestation.
  • Neither manifestation can be turned or actually harmed: they have energy factors but no hit points. They are destroyed if the demilich is; otherwise they remain, losing 1 energy factor per day if left alone until they are gone. The demilich itself cannot be turned either.

Touching the skull: anyone foolish enough to touch it starts a new attack, besides any manifestation.

  1. Howl: the skull rises into the air and gives a howl equal to a death ray in a 20-foot radius. All within must save vs. spell or be permanently slain and forever dead. It senses which member of the party is most powerful, and usually ranks a magic-user over a fighter, a fighter over a cleric, and a cleric over a thief.
  2. Soul drain: the next round, it uses one of the 5-8 gems set in its eye sockets and in place of teeth to draw the soul of the strongest intruder into the jewel. No saving throw is possible. The body collapses and moulders away in a single round. An amulet of life protection defeats the gem’s life-stealing power, but the body still perishes.
  3. The skull then sinks down, sated. Struck or touched again, it rises, howls, and drains the next strongest character into another gem, and so on as long as it is intact and disturbed.
  4. Curses: once all its jewels are full, only the killing howl remains, but it can also curse the remaining intruders. Such curses are very powerful: always to be hit by any attacker, never to make a saving throw, or always to lose all treasure without gaining any experience from it. Remove curse lifts one, but the character’s charisma drops permanently by 1 point (magical increase of charisma is still possible).

Destroying the skull: the monster is only exterminated if its skull is destroyed. The skull has 50 hit points and armor class −6, and can be harmed only as follows:

  • Forget or exorcise: makes it sink down without howling or taking a soul.
  • Shatter: 3-18 points of damage.
  • Power word kill spoken by an astral or ethereal magic-user: destroys it.
  • A fighter or ranger with a vorpal blade, sword of sharpness, sword +5, or vorpal weapon, or a paladin with a vorpal weapon or a +4 or better weapon: full normal damage.
  • Dispel evil: 5-8 points of damage.
  • Holy word: 5-30 points of damage.
  • Any character with a +4 or better magic weapon or a mace of disruption: 1 point of damage per hit.

Trapped souls: when the skull is destroyed, each gem holding a soul makes a saving throw vs. spell as if the trapped character were making it. Gems that fail are empty: the demilich devoured those souls before it was destroyed. A gem that succeeds still holds the soul, shown by a faint inner light, or a tiny figure seen inside with true seeing, true sight, or a gem of seeing. Crushing the gem frees the soul, but some body must be within 10 feet and ready to receive it, such as a clone, a simulacrum, or a soulless body.

Finishing the job: the dust and any other remains must be destroyed with holy water, or the demilich re-forms in 1-10 days.

system.description:
The farastu, or tarry demodand, is tall and slender, fast but the weakest of its kind. Farastu are the commoners of Tarterus.

  • Attacks: long-nailed hands and huge jaws.
  • Tar: its tarry skin oozes, so anything it hits, or that hits it, has a 5% chance of sticking for 1-6 segments. Then: (a) if the farastu stuck itself to an opponent, it gets another attack sequence at once; (b) if an opponent stuck to it by its own attack, and melee runs into a new round because the farastu already attacked that round, the farastu gains the initiative and attacks at +4; (c) if an opponent’s weapon or similar object sticks to it, there is a 25% chance the object is pulled from the opponent’s grasp, and the farastu gains the initiative next round.
  • Spell-like powers (at will, one at a time, one per round, at 11th level): detect good, detect invisibility, detect magic, dispel magic (twice per day), ESP, fascinate, fog cloud (3 times per day), gaseous form, invisibility, tongues, and weakness (reverse of strength, 3 times per day).
  • Summoning: 1-2 more tarry demodands, only on the Planes of Tarterus, 40% chance of success; all farastu together can summon at most 12.
  • Defenses: harmed only by +1 or better magic weapons. Acid and poison have no effect; cold and fire do only half damage. Fear magic and illusion magic (illusion and/or phantasm) are useless against it. Fear is virtually unknown to it.
  • Senses: infravision and ultravision of the sort normal for monsters.

Description: humanoid, with long arms and heads. Effective strength 19; weight about 420 pounds.

Demodands: general (MMII)

The many planes of abysmal Tarterus are the only home of the winged, three-part race of demodands. Where they live, even nycadaemons tread carefully, for demodands are powerful, clever, and cruelly ruthless in their selfish evil. Their society is feudal, of barons and commoners.

Only a single demodand is met on the Prime Material Plane, since they stay in Tarterus, the Abyss, or Hades unless magically brought to another plane, perhaps as a guardian or executioner.

Summoning limit: the total number of demodands of a type summoned to one area by others of that type can never be more than the number of that type met on the Planes of Tarterus: 12, 10, or 8.

The kelubar, or slime demodand, is shorter and thicker-built than a farastu. Though ebon in color, it glistens with a slimy skin secretion. Kelubar are the middle class of Tarterus.

  • Attacks: nails and jaws. Each hit does 1-6 extra points of acid damage from the slime unless the victim saves vs. poison (or is otherwise unaffected by acid).
  • Enslime: if all 3 of its attacks in a round hit, it has grappled and enslimed the victim, which takes 4-24 more points of acid damage: 2-8/2-8/4-16/4-24 in all. A successful saving throw halves the acid damage.
  • Spell-like powers (at will, one at a time, one per round, at 13th level): detect good, detect invisibility, detect magic, dispel magic (3 times per day), ESP, fascinate, fog cloud (3 times per day), gaseous form, invisibility, ray of enfeeblement (once per day), tongues, and weakness (reverse of strength, 3 times per day).
  • Summoning: 1-2 of its fellows, on the Plane of Tarterus, 50% chance of success; at most 10 kelubar can be brought by any one.
  • Defenses: only +2 or better magic weapons harm it. Acid and poison have no effect; cold and fire do only half damage. Fear magic and illusion magic (illusion and/or phantasm) are useless against it. Fear is virtually unknown to it.
  • Senses: infravision to 120 feet and standard ultravision.

Description: humanoid, thickest in the lower body and limbs, with very large hands and huge oval heads, wider than they are tall. Effective strength 20; weight about 490 pounds.

The great shator, or shaggy demodand, is the most fearsome of its kind: the shortest and broadest, with a hide that hangs in overlapping patches, which gives it its name. Shators are the ruling nobility of Tarterus.

  • Attacks: it can deal massive damage with nails and jaws, but it is also dexterous enough to use large weapons (footman’s mace, bastard sword, etc.), at +4 to hit and +9 strength bonus, but then with only 1 attack per round.
  • Tactics: it fully understands its options and always takes the most intelligent plan of attack, which means using its spell-like powers first whenever it can.
  • Spell-like powers (at will, one at a time, one per round, at 15th level): beguile (as a rod of beguiling, once per day), cloudkill (once per day), detect good, detect invisibility, detect magic, dispel magic (3 times per day), ESP, fog cloud (3 times per day), gaseous form, invisibility, ray of enfeeblement (once per day), stinking cloud (once per day), tongues, and weakness (reverse of strength, 3 times per day).
  • Summoning: 1-8 of its fellows, on the Plane of Tarterus, 60% chance of success.
  • Defenses: only +3 or better magic weapons harm it. Its overlapping hide gives edged weapons (long, broad, bastard, and two-handed swords, but not short swords) −1 to hit and damage. Acid and poison have no effect; cold and fire do only half damage. Fear magic and illusion magic (illusion and/or phantasm) are useless against it.
  • Senses: excellent hearing and smell; with these and its sight (infravision and ultravision included), it is surprised only 10% of the time.

Description: 6 feet tall, squat, and broad, its humanoid form seemingly draped in shaggy skins. The huge head is mostly mouth, with jaws like a giant bulldog’s. Effective strength 21; weight around 560 pounds.

system.description:
Alu-demons are the offspring of succubi and humans, and are always female. About 20% are not totally devoted to evil.

  • Armor: their demonic heritage gives a good base armor class, which magic protection, including enchanted armor, can improve. Mundane protection interferes with their natural protection, so they never wear it. If the armor is basically worse than the wearer’s own armor class, only its magic bonus is added; otherwise it gives full benefit. So +1 leather adds only +1, while +1 plate mail makes the armor class 2. High dexterity gives them bonuses as for a normal human.
  • Magic-users: 25% are of genius intelligence and are actual magic-users of 1st-12th level (equal chance of each), on top of their natural powers. The rest have only the limited powers below.
  • Natural powers (one at a time, one per round, each up to 3 times per day, at 12th level): charm person, ESP, shape change (only to a humanoid form of about their own height and weight), and suggestion. Dimension door once per day. All have superior infravision to 240 feet.
  • Weapons: they can use any kind of weapon, whatever the normal class limits.
  • Energy drain: at will, by a firm touch (a successful to-hit roll in melee), they drain 1-8 hit points of life energy and use half (1-4, fractions rounded up) to restore their own lost hit points.
  • Defenses: harmed only by cold-wrought iron or magic weapons; they have natural magic resistance.

Description: quite human, with only small, vestigial horns; only their rather small bat wings show what they really are.

Demons: general (MMII)

Each type of demon, especially the high-level demon lords and princes, has many unusual traits and extraordinary abilities. What all demons share is covered here; more is in the MM under “Demon”, and each demon’s own entry gives the specifics.

  • Travel: demons can move from their own plane into Tarterus, Hades, or Pandemonium, or roam the Astral Plane. They cannot enter the Prime Material Plane without help (conjuration, gate, speaking their name, or similar means). They often roam the Astral and Ethereal Planes, where persons in an ethereal state draw their attention.
  • Nature: chaotic and evil; the smarter and stronger rule the weaker and less intelligent of their kind. The less intelligent attack without question and fight until slain. No demon can ever be subdued. All can divide their attacks among 2 or even 3 opponents if their means allow.
  • Service: demons never serve anyone willingly. Forced by magic or threat, they constantly seek a way to kill their master or captor. Those a demon takes a liking to are usually carried off to its plane as a slave (if a favored one). Characters of any alignment can summon demons, but controlling one is another matter. A thaumaturgic circle keeps out lesser demons; greater demons need a special pentacle. The DM must handle carefully any threat or reward used to win a demon’s service. Holy (good) relics and artifacts repel demons.
  • Names: speaking the name of a particularly powerful demon gives a chance (base 5% recommended) that he hears it and turns his attention to the speaker. Unless ready to avoid that attention or control the demon, the character should know the demon will at once kill whoever spoke his name, by the quickest means.
  • Telepathy: a special form lets demons understand every intelligent communication; those of average or better intelligence can also converse.

No encounter percentages are given, since a layer usually has other creatures too. Demogorgon’s several layers hold many kinds of vicious apes, reptiles (dinosaurs included), and bird-like monsters. Juiblex’s plane has slimes, deadly puddings, jellies, and various amoeboid monsters. Orcus’s many layers are peopled with skeletal monsters, various zombies, huecuva, shadows, sheet phantoms, vampires, and death knights. Yeenoghu’s vast plane abounds with hyenas and hyaenodons, gnolls, ghasts, ghouls, and possibly a few trolls. Other planes hold insects, arachnids, worms and slugs, fungi and fungoid monsters, and so on.

Some layers lack most of the usual inhabitants. The liquid plane ruled by Dagon, for instance, has hezrou (type II) and a kind of dretch, but otherwise octopi, squids, kraken, sea snakes, eels, weird fish, and horrible fish-monsters. In short, use your imagination and creativity to develop these areas.

system.description:
The babau, also called the one-horned horror or ebony death, is tall and looks like a skeleton in skin-tight black leather. Its feet, hands, and head are as large as a hill giant’s, its taloned fingers are deadly, and a horn-like growth juts from the back of its skull, curving forward and down.

  • Tactics: quite clever, it prefers a weapon (missiles, magic, etc.) to its natural attacks if that gives it the advantage. It has 19 strength and uses it to the full. Its favorite attack is to leap on victims from above. It has the abilities of a 9th-level thief.
  • Slime: in combat it oozes a reddish slime over its whole body, so cutting, stabbing, and similar attacks do only half damage as weapons slide off. All weapon forms harm it, though, and cold-wrought iron does +2 points per hit.
  • Darkness: within a 5-foot radius.
  • At will (1 per melee round): fear (by touch only), levitate (as a 10th-level magic-user), fly (as an 11th-level magic-user), dispel magic (as a 12th-level magic-user), polymorph self, heat metal (as a 14th-level druid), and gate in another babau (25% chance of success).
  • Gaze: any creature looking into its glowing red eyes within 20 feet must save vs. spell or be affected as by ray of enfeeblement.

Vrock, hezrou, and glabrezu hate babau. Type IV demons especially hate and fear them in numbers, since babau detest type IV demons except as food.

Baphomet is lord of minotaurs, shaped like a huge bull-headed ogre. Yeenoghu particularly hates him, and the two are at war.

  • Attacks: he first butts and bites, then uses his huge bardiche for 11-20 (3d4+8) points of damage. Armor, shields, and other items it strikes must save vs. crushing blow or be ruined.
  • Minotaurs: 75% likely to have 2-5 with him. Once per day he can summon 5-8 more, possibly in a single round.
  • At will (once per round): darkness (10’ radius), detect invisible, detect magic, dispel magic, levitate, maze (3 times per day), passwall (3 times per day), phantasmal force, shape change (3 times per day), telekinesis (75,000 gp weight), teleport, wall of stone (3 times per day).
  • Bellow (once per day): all creatures within 30” must save vs. spell or flee in panic for 6 rounds.
  • Unholy water (6 times per day): a gout of 1 quart, range 1”, doing 16-64 points of damage to creatures of the Upper or Positive Planes.
  • Gate: a type III demon once per day (85% chance of success).
  • Senses and speech: infravision to 120 feet and hearing twice the human norm. He speaks the minotaur tongue and Common, with limited telepathic communication with animals.

The bar-lgura, or leaping demon, is like an orangutan except for its gruesome face and tusks, and hands and feet with 6 digits bearing exceptionally long claws. system.description:
When a human female mates with a demon, the child is always a cambion male. A cambion’s traits and abilities depend on its parentage: a major cambion, or a baron or marquis.

MajorBaron/Marquis
Armor class (base)62
Hit dice5-89-16
Strength17-18*18-20**
Intelligence9-1613-18
Wisdom5-83-18
Dexterity13-1815-20
Constitution13-1815-18
Charisma1-62-24***
Special defensesNil+1 or better weapon to hit
Magic resistance5%-20%25%-40%
Psionic abilityNilAs human
Attack/defense modesNil/nilAs human
Level/X.P. valueVII/1275 +10/hpBaron: VIII/4409 +15/hp (VIII/4400 in the stat block); Marquis: IX/6500 +20/hp

* Roll d4: 1 = 17, 2 = 18, 3 = 18/10%, 4 = 18/20%. Exceptional strength rolls over 18/00 equal 19.
** Roll d12 and multiply by 10 for an added base for exceptional strength (10% to 120%), then roll percentile dice: 101%-199% = 19 strength, 200%-220% = 20 strength.
*** Scores over 18 mean the cambion can, at will, cause an awe (revulsion) reaction worth as many negative charisma points as exceed 18 (1-6).

A marquis has evil cleric abilities and 16-18 hit dice.

  • Armor: armor class depends on the armor worn and dexterity, but the base is 6 or 2 (by parentage) rather than the normal 10.
  • All cambions: infravision, speech with demons, and the same weakness to iron as normal demons; silver does not harm them.
  • Major cambions: few other abilities. Those with intelligence over 14 can, with proper training, practice magic up to 5th level, on top of fighting as a monster of their hit dice. They can also become thieves or assassins of a level equal to their hit dice. Their hit dice never exceed the maximum set at birth, 5-8 (d4+4).
  • Barons and marquises: 1-4 of these abilities: cause fear by touch, detect magic, levitate (at magic-user level equal to half their hit dice), and polymorph self. They fight as fighters of their hit dice (9th-16th level). Those with wisdom over 9 can, with proper training, become evil clerics of a level up to their total hit dice; they can also become assassins up to that level. Each profession other than fighter must be followed in turn, not at the same time.

Description: 6-7½ feet tall, stocky and strong. Many have demonic features such as an odd-colored complexion, scaly skin, misshapen ears, fangs, or small horns; there is no set pattern, and cambions vary in appearance nearly as much as humans.

system.description:
The chasme, or fly demon, is a particularly loathsome monster, like a cross between a common fly and a human. It stands on 4 fly-like hind legs and grasps with its forelimbs, which have strong, chitinous pincer fingers. It has wings and the blue-black, hairy body of a fly, and like a fly can walk on walls and ceilings. Its head is humanoid, with saucer eyes and a mane of stiff, swept-back bristles. The mouth is tiny, but the sharp, horn-like nose is used to bite and draw blood.

  • Minor demon powers: infravision, darkness (5-foot radius), and teleport.
  • At will (one at a time): detect good, detect invisible, telekinesis (1,500 gp weight).
  • Touch: causes fear as a wand.
  • Drone: at all times except when using spell-like powers, it can buzz and drone in a horrid, rasping voice. Each round, each opponent has a chance (100% minus 10% per level or hit die) of falling into a comatose sleep. Sleepers must be splashed with water or vigorously roused to wake; otherwise they sleep 2-8 hours or until the chasme drains their blood for 1-4 points of damage.
  • Defenses: normal weapons can strike it, but poison does not affect it.
  • Gate: if hard pressed, it tries to gate in another of its kind (15% chance of success).

Chasme hate most other demons, especially the stupid vrock and hezrou, but are smart enough to avoid fighting other demons unless they have the advantage. Rutterkin are allied with chasme, though chasme are not fond of rutterkin and use them.

Description: round, rubbery bodies with thin, spindly arms and legs, and small heads set squarely on the shoulders. Sparse, bristly hair; floppy ears sticking out; eyes slanting down; a squashed-looking nose; and a slack, slobbering mouth with many small fangs.

This huge monster has a storm giant’s strength.

  • Attacks: each powerful fist does 13-18 points of damage, and he can bite any opponent he is holding for 3-18. His 15-foot, razor-barbed tail can slash for 1-12, or wrap around and lift a victim so he can bite or hit it.
  • At will (at 20th level, one at a time): darkness (30-foot radius), dispel magic, polymorph others or self, hypnotic pattern, misdirection, suggestion, programmed illusion, telekinesis of 10,000 gp weight, teleport, or veil.
  • Once per day (one per round): prismatic spray, plane shift, power word blind.
  • Gate or deceive: he can gate in 1-4 type I demons (60% chance of success), but is 75% likely to choose instead to trick another demon prince or princess into believing he or she has been summoned (75% chance of making one appear). The arriving demon lord will be furious to find himself tricked, and it is 85% likely the creatures nearby will suffer, since the Prince of Deception will have gone elsewhere.
  • Defenses: 70% magic resistance, and completely resistant to spells that detect or influence (charm, command, dominate, hypnotize, suggest, etc.).
  • Speech: all known human tongues, and telepathy with most other creatures.

His plane: an Abyssal plane that seems totally flat and featureless, but is actually alive to his wishes and shapes itself into hills, caves, and so on. By the account of the 2 people who went there and returned, it is not only depressing and sickening but drains magic items of their dweomer (as shown by the loss of the swords of utmost prowess they carried). So though he surely has great treasure (O, P, S, T, U, Z), it is 90% certain that its magic items other than artifacts and relics are spoiled.

History: for several centuries he was trapped in a stone prison in the dungeons beneath Castle Greyhawk (see the WORLD OF GREYHAWK™ set). Many adventurers unwise enough to talk with him were destroyed forever, but in the end 2 powerful characters, a magic-user and a cleric, were tricked into a series of heroic deeds that set him free; both were carried off to his plane as slaves. Enraged at his long torment, he has sworn vengeance on all humankind. He is searching for his staff, a powerful instrument said to combine the powers of a staff of command, a rod of beguiling, and a rod of rulership. It was stolen from him while he was imprisoned, and even the other demon princes do not want it found.

Description: a hulking body covered with short, coarse hair, broad splayed feet, and very large, stubby hands. His face is beautiful but cruel, with a huge, fanged mouth, and large, ragged ears rise from the middle of his domed, rather pointed head. Pale blue hair, grayish skin, and 2 vast dull black wings. His hairless tail shades from gray at the base to pale blue at the tip.

Juiblex’s plane has slimes, deadly puddings, jellies, and various amoeboid monsters. Orcus’s many layers are peopled with skeletal monsters, various zombies, huecuva, shadows, sheet phantoms, vampires, and death knights. Yeenoghu’s vast plane abounds with hyenas and hyaenodons, gnolls, ghasts, ghouls, and possibly a few trolls. In short, use your imagination and creativity to develop these areas.

Graz’zt, lord of an entire layer of the Abyss, is one of the most powerful demon rulers and a sworn foe of both Demogorgon and Orcus. He was in fact winning a war against the troglodyte, harpy, and bar-lgura when, at the crucial moment, a mighty magic-user magically took him to the Prime Material Plane and bound him in servitude. He fought free at the cost of being confined to his own plane for a century.

  • Servants: always 1-3 lamias with him; in his lair he is also likely to have 1-3 succubi or a type VI demoness.
  • Weapons: normally a huge +3 shield and a huge wavy-bladed sword (equal to a bastard sword) that drips acid on command, for 5-8 extra points of damage. On a natural 20 to hit, the target’s non-living possessions must save vs. acid. His other weapon is a +1 guisarme.
  • Two weapons: using 2 weapons instead of a shield doubles his normal attacks, but his armor class goes from −9 to −6.
  • At will (1 per melee round, at 20th level): alter reality for another, chaos, continual darkness, disintegrate (once per day), dispel magic, duo-dimension, emotion, magic missile (5 missiles), mirror image, polymorph any object (once per day), polymorph (twice per day), polymorph self, read languages, read magic, telekinesis of 15,000 gp weight, teleport, trap the soul (once per week), vanish, veil (once per day), water breathing.
  • Fear: by sneer and word, he causes fear in all within 60 feet who see and hear his displeasure.
  • Gate: 1-2 type VI demons (60%) or 2-5 babau (40%), without fail.

Description: the handsomest of demon rulers, at least by human standards: a huge, good-looking man, but with shining black skin and glowing green eyes. His pointed ears and small fangs merely hint at his alien nature. He has 6 fingers and 6 toes.

Kostchtchie is a powerful demon lord so hateful that even the rest of his kind dislike him, except the minor demons.

  • Strength: very great, with a matching bonus to damage.
  • Weapon: his favorite is a huge cold-iron hammer inlaid with nickel and silver (2-12 points of damage). An opponent it hits must save vs. paralysis or be stunned, unable to act for the rest of that round and all of the next.
  • Guards: a pair of the largest leucrotta are his constant guards and companions (AC 3; MV 18”; HD 9; hp 2×49; #AT 1; D 8-18; SD rear kicks, 2 for 2-7 hp damage each).
  • At will (one at a time, one per round, at 20th level): command, curse, darkness (15-foot radius), dispel good, harm (once per day), know alignment, poison (twice per day), protection from good (10-foot radius), speak with monsters, teleport, telekinesis of 5,000 gp weight, unholy word (once per day), and wind walk (twice per day).
  • Gate: always succeeds: 1-4 babau (35%) or 2-5 bar-lgura (65%).
  • Speech: many languages, and telepathy.

Frost giants sometimes serve him. He is rumored to have an ancient white dragon of the largest size as his steed.

Description: like a giant with short, bandy, malformed legs, so he moves fairly slowly. A flat, oval head with slitted eyes and gross features; a torso and arms bulging with muscle. His skin is pale yellow and hairless except for the eyebrows.

Nabassu, or death stealers, are demons that live on the Prime Material Plane for a time. Living in desolate places, they constantly trouble mankind with raids to work their great evil, feeding their lust for cruelty and their wish to regain their place in the Abyss.

Life cycle: to grow and mature, each must kill many humans, create evil undead, and work wickedness. After hatching, each spends a time in the Abyss; those that survive to young adulthood must come to the Prime Material Plane, which they do by an inborn ability to use psionic probability travel, though they have no other psionic ability. They can take others with them this way. Many die on the journey, but a few live to begin their growth.

  • Growth: demonlings arrive with only armor class 4 and 5 hit dice, gaining 2 hit points from the journey. After that, each human they kill and devour adds 1 hit point and improves armor class by half a point, so after 2 humans a nabassu has +4 hit points and armor class 3. After 18 humans it is fully grown and can return to its own plane and set up a comfortable domain (always within a year or two of maturity).
  • Treasure: on the Prime Material Plane they hoard only gems, jewelry, and magic items in their lairs (Q×5, each checked separately, and F magic). In the Abyss each has type H, guarded by several lesser vassal demons.

Powers: besides claws and bite, they have magical powers of attack and defense, each usable at will, one at a time, one per round.

  • Immature nabassu: cause shadows (20-foot radius, making dim, shadowy light except in darkness), shed darkness (5-foot radius), and a death-stealing gaze usable once per hit point it has gained above its 5 hit dice. Shadows and darkness last as long as it wishes or until dispelled.
  • Death stealing (range 2”): the victim must save vs. death magic or become a ghast (a ghoul if demi-human or humanoid) under the nabassu’s control as soon as it dies or is slain.
  • Bestowing death (range 1”): the nabassu can then give the stolen death to anyone who fails a save vs. death magic, killing him at once. The victim becomes a shadow (unless already subjected to death stealing) doomed to serve the nabassu whenever called. Exorcising the corpse (with or without restoring life) avoids this doom.
  • Thief abilities: move silently, hide in shadows, hear noise, and strike from behind, at a thief level equal to half its hit point bonus.
  • Defenses: harmed only by iron or +1 or better magic weapons.
  • Coloring: it can change from brown-black to pale dove gray and any shade between, letting it hide in shadows or against a matching background.
  • Strength: effective 18/00.

At maturity it gains: summon 2-5 ghasts (once per day, in the Abyss), energy drain, etherealness (twice per day), paralyzation (10-foot radius, once per day), regenerate up to 20 hit points per day, silence (10-foot radius, once per day), teleportation, and vampiric attack (once per day, range 2”). Vampiric attack drains whatever power, physical or magical, the opponent is using at the time and turns it against him; the opponent cannot use it that round, and if he strikes successfully the effect happens to him instead of the nabassu.

Description: tall and thin, with scaly, sinewy bodies. A very long head with small horns, long bat-like ears, and tusk-like teeth in a huge mouth; the other features are small, and the eyes glow yellow. Long fingers end in long, razor-sharp talons. The wings are bat-like but scaled. They can color themselves from near-black through brown to palest dove gray.

name: Pazuzu (Prince of the Lower Aerial Kingdoms)

system.treasure: S, T, U, V, W, X, Z
system.psionicText: 255 Attack/Defense Modes: All/immune to psionic attacks
system.description:
Pazuzu, or Pazzuzeus, is unlike all other lords of the Abyss: he rules, at least to some degree, the skies above all its layers. He competes for rule of no plane or place, considering himself above competition, and treats all the powers of the Lower Planes equally (if not actually as equals). He travels freely throughout the Lower Outer Planes and is on friendly terms with mighty daemons and the dukes of Hell. He can also enter the Prime Material Plane at will, whether by his own power or some secret artifact is uncertain. He is lord of all evil flying creatures, and those under 5 hit dice obey his every command if he is within their sight.

Corrupting the good: his main efforts are on the Prime Material Plane, where he uses his powers to gain followers and servants. His special joy is turning lawful good clerics and paladins to his service. First he gets them to speak his name aloud 3 times in a row. This does not yet change their alignment, but brings him to the speaker. He explains that the summoner may call on him for aid at any time, and may ask a service at once or demand it after giving aid. Doing anything he asks or demands changes the servant’s alignment. Such acts tend toward chaos but not always outright evil; though chaotic, he helps those who obey and serve him if it suits him or amuses him. Naturally, the more often service is given, the greater the evil and the more evil the servant becomes.

He is said to have a great sense of humor, and has sometimes not taken offense at a check or defeat, especially if his opponents were clever enough to outwit him.

  • At will (besides the usual demon powers; one at a time, one per round): astral travel, call lightning, control weather, darkness (20-foot radius), flesh to stone, shape change, statue, symbol (1 each of pain, hopelessness, death), tongues, unholy word, wind walk, and wish (once per day).
  • Breath (3 times per day, one of each): creeping doom, insect plague, and poison gas (the size of a green dragon’s breath).
  • Defense: he seldom uses a weapon, preferring to send in his bodyguard (usually 6 type VI demons, not those listed in the MM) and use his spell-like or mental (psionic) powers. With 90% probability he can summon 4-16 harpies (50%), 3-12 perytons (25%), or 3-12 gargoyles (25%).
  • Gate: 1-4 succubi with 75% probability, once per day.
  • Style: he would rather play with and torment victims and opponents than use drastic attacks, except in life or death situations.
  • Other: double normal infravision and ultravision; regenerates 1 hit point per round.

Description: he can appear as nearly any creature, usually a human or some creature of the air. In his true form he is a tall humanoid with 4 wings, handsome but with features that betray great evil, and glowing red eyes. He has a noble brow, a large head, a solid, muscular body, and taloned, bird-like feet.

Demons: general (MMII)

Each type of demon, especially the high-level demon lords and princes, has many unusual traits and extraordinary abilities. What all demons share is covered here; more is in the MM under “Demon”, and each demon’s own entry gives the specifics.

They cannot enter the Prime Material Plane without help (conjuration, gate, speaking their name, or similar means). They often roam the Astral and Ethereal Planes, where persons in an ethereal state draw their attention.
  • Nature: chaotic and evil; the smarter and stronger rule the weaker and less intelligent of their kind. The less intelligent attack without question and fight until slain. No demon can ever be subdued. All can divide their attacks among 2 or even 3 opponents if their means allow.
  • Service: demons never serve anyone willingly. Forced by magic or threat, they constantly seek a way to kill their master or captor. Those a demon takes a liking to are usually carried off to its plane as a slave (if a favored one). Characters of any alignment can summon demons, but controlling one is another matter. A thaumaturgic circle keeps out lesser demons; greater demons need a special pentacle. The DM must handle carefully any threat or reward used to win a demon’s service. Holy (good) relics and artifacts repel demons.

Unless ready to avoid that attention or control the demon, the character should know the demon will at once kill whoever spoke his name, by the quickest means.

No encounter percentages are given, since a layer usually has other creatures too. Demogorgon’s several layers hold many kinds of vicious apes, reptiles (dinosaurs included), and bird-like monsters. Juiblex’s plane has slimes, deadly puddings, jellies, and various amoeboid monsters. Orcus’s many layers are peopled with skeletal monsters, various zombies, huecuva, shadows, sheet phantoms, vampires, and death knights. Yeenoghu’s vast plane abounds with hyenas and hyaenodons, gnolls, ghasts, ghouls, and possibly a few trolls. Other planes hold insects, arachnids, worms and slugs, fungi and fungoid monsters, and so on.

Some layers lack most of the usual inhabitants. The liquid plane ruled by Dagon, for instance, has hezrou (type II) and a kind of dretch, but otherwise octopi, squids, kraken, sea snakes, eels, weird fish, and horrible fish-monsters. In short, use your imagination and creativity to develop these areas.

Rutterkin are among the weakest but most bullying of demons. Whether they truly think themselves superior or swagger to make up for their inferiority does not matter. Most demons hate and abuse them, and they return the favor whenever they can, especially against a dretch, a lone vrock, or a single hezrou.

Weapons: their clubbed fists are fair weapons, but they prefer strange polearms and weird weapons. Favorites:

  • Snap-tongs: 2-8 points on a hit, and the same each round after until the opponent breaks free (by spending a round not attacking and rolling as if to hit).
  • Polearm with a double crescent head: S-M 1-10, L 1-12.
  • Saw-toothed flatchet: as a broad sword, +1 damage against unarmored opponents.
  • Three-armed blades thrown from an atlatl-like device: S-M 3-8, L 3-6, range 15”.
  • At will (once per round): darkness (5-foot radius), fear by touch, fly, telekinesis (1,000 gp weight), teleport (once per day).
  • Gate: chasmes (15% chance of success), their only demon allies.

system.description:
The derro are a degenerate race of dwarf-like height, possibly a cross between evil humans and dwarves. They live in the great underground realms shared by drow and their ilk (kuo-toans, mind flayers, troglodytes, etc.). They hate light and are nauseated by sunlight, but they come up at night through secret shafts to steal and kidnap humans as slaves; rumor says some are eaten as well. They are said to have a major stronghold somewhere deep underground, where their savants plot to devastate the upper world and enslave all mankind.

  • Dexterity: high (15-18), so adjust armor class to match.
  • Senses: poor infravision (30 feet) but good ultravision (120 feet).
  • Languages: their own, some Common, and the trade tongue of the underground world.

Arms and armor:

ChanceArmorWeapons
40-50%Studded leatherRepeating light crossbow (12” maximum range, 2 shots per round, 6-bolt magazine, 1-3 points of damage; derro poison on the bolts adds 2-12 points unless a save is made)
20-30%Studded leatherHook fauchard (over 6 feet long, 1-4 points of damage, 25% likely to pull a man-sized or smaller victim off balance) and dagger
10-20%Scaled leather (dragon hide or the like, equal to mail)Dagger, spiked buckler (attacks as a dagger), and aklys (spiked and hooked, half as effective as a hook fauchard at pulling opponents down or off balance)
10-20%Scaled leatherBuckler, spear, and leather pick (damage as a military pick)
  • Leaders: 1 of 4 hit dice for every 3 derro, and 1 of 5 hit dice for every 6. With 10 or more, a 7 hit dice leader and a 6 hit dice lieutenant. All are in addition to the number rolled, wear scaled leather, and have superior weapons. With 20 or more, there is also a savant and 2 student savants.
  • Lair: always 30 plus 3-12 normal derro, the matching higher-level leaders, 1-3 savants, 2-5 student savants, 15-40 slaves (80% female), and as allies 1-3 gargoyles (70%) or a lamia (30%).

Savants: sage-like derro who can use any kind of magic item and weapon. Savants have 5-8 hit dice and know 6-9 spells; their apprentices, the student savants (or students), have 4-7 hit dice, know 1-3 spells, study only a minor field, and are only 25% likely to be able to use a non-fighter magic item. All can comprehend languages and read magic, and perform at 12th level of ability.

  • Spells: affect normal fires, anti-magic shell, blink, light, lightning bolt, minor creation, charm person, cloudkill, ESP, hypnotic pattern, ice storm, invisibility, levitate, paralyzation, repulsion, shadow magic, spider climb, ventriloquism, wall of fog, wall of force.
  • Magic items: savants have 2-3 useful (and used) offensive and/or defensive items, students 1 lesser item. Typical items: any potion; any scroll; rings of fire resistance, invisibility, protection, and spell storing; any wand; studded leather +1 armor and shields; any swords up to +3; bracers of defense, brooch of shielding, cloak of protection, etc.; and any miscellaneous weapons.

Description: very much like humans, but shorter and slightly more muscular for their height, with features tending to grossness. Hair pale tan or yellow, skin very white with a bluish undertone, and very large eyes.

system.description:
Astral devas serve mainly on the Astral Plane or any of the outer Lower Planes, moving about alone or in groups in their sovereigns’ service. They are very quick, on foot or flying on their mighty wings.

  • Weapon: usually a huge, mace-like weapon, wielded nimbly, of +3 value in an astral deva’s hands. A creature struck twice in the same round and taking over 20 hit points of damage must save vs. spell or be knocked senseless for 14 rounds. The weapon also acts as a mace of disruption (q.v.), with chances as if wielded by a 9th-level cleric.
  • Spell-like powers: those given above, at will, 1 per round, to the stated limits. Its light can have a 4-40 foot radius as it wishes. Its protection from evil is a sphere of 10-foot radius and normal (+2) power. It can also dispel illusion, dispel invisibility of any sort, polymorph self, or remove curse, also 1 per round. Once per day it can create a blade barrier lasting up to 7 turns.
  • Defenses: never surprised. Harmed only by +1 or better magic weapons. Total vacuum does not hurt it. Immune to level loss from undead or magic, and to death spells; its soul cannot be trapped or imprisoned.
  • Charisma effect: 20.

Description: tall, slender, and graceful, with golden skin and hair, amber eyes, and large white wings tinted with gold; otherwise like humans.

Devas: general (MMII)

Devas live in the upper Outer Planes of Good, as servants and messengers of the various good deities: some lawful, some chaotic, some neutral, but all good. They are by no means the most powerful creatures of their planes, but they are certainly powerful servants of Good (compare planetar, solar).

  • Travel: all devas can travel the planes of good alignment, though lawful ones do so only on a deity’s orders, and even chaotic ones seldom travel except in service. All can become ethereal, but only the astral deva can travel astrally unless commanded by a deity. They work equally well in any environment, water included.
  • Death: on the Prime Material Plane or any Elemental Plane, only a deva’s material body can be destroyed. Its spirit cannot be harmed and returns at once to its own plane, where it stays for a decade regaining the power to form a body again. On any other plane, devas can truly die.
  • Dealings: no deva ever negotiates with creatures of evil, though non-lawful devas might strike a bargain with non-evil neutrals.
  • Combat: a deva can usually judge which opponents are most powerful and dangerous, and attack accordingly. It can divide its attacks in a round if it wishes.

Spell-like powers (all devas, one at a time, one per round): cure disease (3 per day), cure light wounds (7 per day), cure serious wounds (3 per day), detect evil, detect illusion, detect magic, detect traps (7 per day), dispel magic (7 per day), etherealness, heal (1 per day), know alignment, invisibility (individual or 10-foot radius), light (effect varies), polymorph self, read magic, remove curse, remove fear, teleport without error, tongues, and ultravision, protection from evil.

Defenses: unaffected by cold, electricity, magic missile, petrification, poison, normal fire, or any gas attack spells. Dragon and magical fire do half damage (monadic devas are unaffected by fire of any kind); acid does full damage. Normal iron or silver weapons do no damage, but magic ones do full damage.

The 3 kinds of devas found anywhere in the Upper Outer Planes are described in their own entries.

Monadic devas usually serve on the Ethereal and Elemental Planes; any environment is home to them.

  • Weapon: usually a metal rod equal to a +2 weapon, used to pierce or smite at up to 10 feet. Very dense creatures (such as one of solid rock) and metal-armored opponents take double damage from any 2nd hit in a single round.
  • Spell-like powers: those given under “Devas”, at will, 1 per round, to the stated limits. Its light can reach 3-30 feet as it wishes. Its protection from evil sphere is half power (+1) but 15-foot radius. Once per round at will it can also hold monster (elementals only, 1 creature, 8 rounds, 3 per day) or project image (1 per day).
  • Defenses: hit only by +1 or better weapons. Immune to level loss from magic or undead and to death magic from any source.
  • Charisma effect: 19.

Description: milky white with silvery hair and colorless eyes, and white wings with a silver sheen; otherwise like very strong humans, broad-shouldered and heroically built.

The 3 kinds of devas found anywhere in the Upper Outer Planes are described in their own entries.

Movanic devas serve mainly on the Material Planes: Negative, Positive, and Prime. Negative or positive power is all the same to them.

  • Weapon: usually a long, slender sword, used fast and skillfully, which generally works as a +1 flame tongue sword for effects and special bonuses to hit and damage.
  • Spell-like powers: those given above, at will, 1 per round, to the stated limits. Its light ranges from 2 to 20 feet as it wishes. Its protection from evil sphere has a 10-foot radius and half (+1) power. At will, once per round, it can also cause or cure blindness, detect traps, and neutralize poison (3 per day).
  • Defenses: harmed only by +1 or better weapons. Plant life of any kind will not (and cannot) harm it, and normal animals will not willingly attack it (reptiles and the like, and “monsters”, may). Immune to death magic, and to level loss, energy drain, and other energy effects of the Negative or Positive Material Planes.
  • Charisma effect: 18.

Abishai, the scaly devils, are common in the First Hell. They are reptilian, and most serve Tiamat. Deeper in Hell they are common on the 1st and 2nd planes, uncommon on the 3rd, rare on the 4th, and very rare on the 5th and 6th.

  • In the lair: always more abishai, and about 10% of the time 1-4 other types with them.
  • Treasure: they do not value treasure, but sometimes (15%) are carrying Q-type treasure to some greater devil.
  • Weapons: the damage shown is for each kind’s weapon, with strength bonus added: black use halberds, white flails, red long daggers, green guisarme-voulges, and blue tridents.
  • Grappling: all can grapple in hand-to-hand combat for 1-4 (cuts from sharp scales, talons, etc.) plus strength bonus: red +1, green or white +2, blue +3, black +4. They can also strike with their tails for 1-2 points.
  • Regeneration: 1 point per round, except for damage from silver, holy water, or holy magic weapons.
  • Spell-like powers (one at a time, one per round): change self, command, produce flame, pyrotechnics, scare, and summon another abishai (20% chance of success, once per day).

Description: the very picture of devils: humanoids with small horns, snaky hair, fangs, pointed ears, slanting eyes, leathery wings, and barbed tails, with scaly hides and reptilian feet.

Devils: general (MMII)

The dwellers and rulers of the planes of Hell are mainly devils, the most powerful of lawful evil creatures. In their traits and abilities they are somewhat like the demons of chaos. Their shared traits are covered here; each type and arch-devil has its own entry, and more is in the MM under “Devil”.

  • Order: devils follow a strict chain of command that they dare not break for fear of the arch-devils. Still, there is great rivalry and open hostility among the devils of the various planes and among the arch-devils. While the lesser devils squabble, the dukes of Hell scheme to seize Asmodeus’s throne, but the archfiend has always played one against another and still rules from his lowest plane.
  • Travel: all devils can move about the planes of Hell (though only the dukes dare do so without authorization), and to Gehenna, Hades, and Acheron at will. They can also move through the Astral Plane, though they seldom do. No devil can enter other planes unless the proper ritual is performed, a gate is opened, or its proper name is spoken (and heard).
  • Death: the material form of a greater devil or duke can be destroyed, but such creatures can only truly be slain if met and fought in Hell or the lower planes next to it. A greater devil whose material form is destroyed is forced into lemure form for 9 decades of torment before it regains its former station. A duke whose material form is destroyed is bound to its own plane of Hell for a decade (unless properly called before the 10 years are up) and suffers a great loss of face.
  • Combat: devils can never be subdued. Lesser ones always fight until destroyed; greater ones will negotiate if seriously threatened. All can direct their attacks at 2 or more opponents if they have the means.
  • Service: devils serve if properly commanded, but it is risky, since an improper command breaks the law that binds them (and it usually takes a contract for the commander’s soul). People other than lawful evil ones can invoke or deal with devils. Properly drawn magic circles (with symbols, for greater and arch-devils) keep devils off for a time. Holy (good) artifacts or relics repel them.
  • Telepathy: a special form lets them understand and converse with any intelligent creature.

Devils: general (MMII)

The dwellers and rulers of the planes of Hell are mainly devils, the most powerful of lawful evil creatures. In their traits and abilities they are somewhat like the demons of chaos. Their shared traits are covered here; each type and arch-devil has its own entry, and more is in the MM under “Devil”.

  • Order: devils follow a strict chain of command that they dare not break for fear of the arch-devils. Still, there is great rivalry and open hostility among the devils of the various planes and among the arch-devils. While the lesser devils squabble, the dukes of Hell scheme to seize Asmodeus’s throne, but the archfiend has always played one against another and still rules from his lowest plane.
  • Travel: all devils can move about the planes of Hell (though only the dukes dare do so without authorization), and to Gehenna, Hades, and Acheron at will. They can also move through the Astral Plane, though they seldom do. No devil can enter other planes unless the proper ritual is performed, a gate is opened, or its proper name is spoken (and heard).
  • Death: the material form of a greater devil or duke can be destroyed, but such creatures can only truly be slain if met and fought in Hell or the lower planes next to it. A greater devil whose material form is destroyed is forced into lemure form for 9 decades of torment before it regains its former station. A duke whose material form is destroyed is bound to its own plane of Hell for a decade (unless properly called before the 10 years are up) and suffers a great loss of face.
  • Combat: devils can never be subdued. Lesser ones always fight until destroyed; greater ones will negotiate if seriously threatened. All can direct their attacks at 2 or more opponents if they have the means.
  • Service: devils serve if properly commanded, but it is risky, since an improper command breaks the law that binds them (and it usually takes a contract for the commander’s soul). People other than lawful evil ones can invoke or deal with devils. Properly drawn magic circles (with symbols, for greater and arch-devils) keep devils off for a time. Holy (good) artifacts or relics repel them.
  • Telepathy: a special form lets them understand and converse with any intelligent creature.

Amon is a vassal of Geryon, raising and commanding up to 40 companies of bone devils from his fief.

  • Fear: anyone he gazes on must save vs. spells or be afraid.
  • Summon: 1-4 bone devils (60% chance of success).
  • Regeneration: 1-12 points of damage per turn.

Bearded devils live in the Third Hell, Mammon’s domain, and the planes below it. They are especially cruel and violent and attack on any excuse. This makes them unpopular and the target of frequent, harsh discipline, but also good shock troops.

  • Glaive: usually a saw-toothed glaive with a treble hook at the base of the blade, curving backward to snag opponents closing in or fleeing (1-3 points of damage, and held fast unless the victim makes a roll as for opening a door).
  • Unarmed: they attack with their wire-like beards and clawed hands. If both hands hit, the beard does maximum damage (8 points), and any creature taking maximum beard damage must save vs. poison or at once develop a burning rash that lowers dexterity by 1 point per round for 4 rounds.
  • At will (one at a time, 1 per turn or round as fits): affect normal fires, command, fear by touch, produce flame, and summon another bearded devil (35% chance of success).

Great Belial rules the Fourth Hell. He is firmly on Baalzebul’s side and hates Geryon nearly as much as Moloch does; he must also guard against Mammon’s schemes, so he is not free to act. From his basalt palace he rules the abishai, barbed, bearded, bone, and spined devils of the reeking fens and smoking plains of his realm. He is also the lord of pain and suffering.

  • Weapon: a huge military fork +4; anyone it strikes must save vs. spells or be affected as by a symbol of pain.
  • At will (one at a time, one per round, as a 20th-level magic-user): animate dead, beguile, charm person, detect magic, dispel illusion, detect invisible, dispel magic, geas, illusion, invisibility, know alignment, light, produce flame, pyrotechnics, raise dead fully, read languages, read magic, shape change, suggestion, teleportation, wall of fire, and granting another’s wish.
  • Limited: a symbol of pain 3 times per day; an unholy word once per day.
  • Fear: anyone he stares at (save vs. spells).
  • Summon (85% chance of success): 1-4 black abishai (25%), 1-3 barbed devils (25%), or 1-4 bearded devils (50%).

Description: the most handsome and most devilish-looking of all devils, with large, slanted, glowing red eyes.

The dwellers and rulers of the planes of Hell are mainly devils, the most powerful of lawful evil creatures. In their traits and abilities they are somewhat like the demons of chaos. Their shared traits are covered here; each type and arch-devil has its own entry, and more is in the MM under “Devil”.

  • Order: devils follow a strict chain of command that they dare not break for fear of the arch-devils. Still, there is great rivalry and open hostility among the devils of the various planes and among the arch-devils. While the lesser devils squabble, the dukes of Hell scheme to seize Asmodeus’s throne, but the archfiend has always played one against another and still rules from his lowest plane.
  • Travel: all devils can move about the planes of Hell (though only the dukes dare do so without authorization), and to Gehenna, Hades, and Acheron at will. They can also move through the Astral Plane, though they seldom do. No devil can enter other planes unless the proper ritual is performed, a gate is opened, or its proper name is spoken (and heard).
  • Death: the material form of a greater devil or duke can be destroyed, but such creatures can only truly be slain if met and fought in Hell or the lower planes next to it. A greater devil whose material form is destroyed is forced into lemure form for 9 decades of torment before it regains its former station. A duke whose material form is destroyed is bound to its own plane of Hell for a decade (unless properly called before the 10 years are up) and suffers a great loss of face.

  • Service: devils serve if properly commanded, but it is risky, since an improper command breaks the law that binds them (and it usually takes a contract for the commander’s soul). People other than lawful evil ones can invoke or deal with devils. Properly drawn magic circles (with symbols, for greater and arch-devils) keep devils off for a time. Holy (good) artifacts or relics repel them.

Mammon is king of Hell’s Third Plane. He and Dispater are supposedly allies who jointly support Mephistopheles, but neither has ever failed to obey Asmodeus, and it is doubtful Mammon really trusts Dispater. His realm is an endless series of rifts with slime streams along their bottoms, and hot ash falls from volcanoes scattered across the badlands. Mephistopheles rules the Eighth Hell. His main aim is to seize the 7th plane from Baalzebul and use the strength gained to challenge Asmodeus for rule of all the hells. His great iron citadel in the ice mountains of the frozen plane is a place of much plotting and intrigue. The plane’s outer marches of oozing slime and the steaming fringe beyond, where his malebranche and pit fiends come from, are said to worry him constantly.

  • Weapon: a great three-tined fork +3 that, on his command, deals 3-12 points of cold, electrical, or fire damage (save vs. spells), each function 3 times per day, on top of its normal damage.

  • Summon: 1-3 ice devils (90% chance of success).

Description: a tall, blue-black humanoid with handsome if devilish features and huge muscles suiting his great strength. His scales are sooty black; his wings, horns, and talons deep blue. His eyes are pale blue with red irises and pupils. His normal speech is a whispering wind.

Moloch is a grand duke, Baalzebul’s viceroy, and lord of Hell’s Sixth Plane. There is great hatred between him and Geryon; without Baalzebul there would be open war between them, much to Moloch’s cost and Mephistopheles’s delight.

  • Attacks: strong as a hill giant, he grabs and crushes or pierces with his huge hands and taloned fingers, then bites with his shark-toothed mouth.
  • Whip: a 6-tailed whip of an unknown, flexible metal. Each tail that strikes does 1, 2, or 4 points of electrical damage, depending on the charges he spends; he can spend up to 20 charges per turn. Lesser devils greatly fear it. (The whip itself holds no charges.)
  • At will (once per turn or round, as a 20th-level magic-user): affect normal fires, animate dead, beguile, burning hands (16 points of damage), detect invisible, detect magic, fire charm, fly, geas, illusion, know alignment, polymorph self, produce fire, produce flame, pyrotechnics, raise dead fully, read languages, read magic, suggestion, teleport without error, wall of fire, and granting another’s limited wish.
  • Once per day: flame strike, a symbol of stunning, and an unholy word.
  • Breath: when he chooses, he can breathe on 1-8 persons within 30 feet; those failing a save vs. breath weapon are so afraid they drop their weapons and flee.
  • Summon: 1-3 horned devils (80% chance of success).

Description: a great, square-bodied creature with red-orange skin, short thick arms and legs, and huge square hands and feet. His feet and huge head are horned, with slanting eyes and a gaping mouth.

Nupperibos exist by the hundreds of thousands throughout the hells. They are the remains of all lawful evil creatures not wicked enough to become lemures (q.v.). They are blind, deaf, and mute, but sense mental commands from stronger devils and the presence of their own kind. They obey every command readily, to lessen the pain and torment that is the normal lot in the infernal regions.

  • Attacks: normally 2 raking claws. When an infernal army gathers, each is given a weapon, usually a club, spear, or polearm. They march and attack blindly but effectively, in vast legions directed by more powerful devils. If not commanded, the hordes keep marching and attacking everything not of the Nine Hells.
  • Regeneration: 1 hit point per round in the infernal regions or areas of total evil, but not elsewhere, and not against holy objects (water, weapons).
  • Re-forming: nupperibos slain in the cause of evil are 99% likely to be re-formed as nupperibos, with a 1% chance of becoming special lemures, the kind lesser devils are made from. Spending a mere thousand years as one of these, a creature might become a devil.
  • Intelligence: with their limited senses no intelligence as such can be assigned; were their state changed, it could range from semi- to exceptional.

Titivilus is notorious for twisting words, using words to confuse, and confusing those who use words. Fittingly, he is Dispater’s messenger. He is not large or especially strong, but most clever. He is said to have a silver sword of wounding, but normally uses his other powers.

  • At will (1 per round, as a 20th-level magic-user): animate dead, bestow curse, charm person or mammal, chaos, emotion, feeblemind (once per day), forget, fumble, hypnotism, illusion, illusionary script, improved invisibility, know alignment, message, misdirection, nondetection, polymorph self, protection from good, suggestion, teleport, tongues, ventriloquism, whispering wind.
  • Once per day: a symbol of discord, or sleep affecting 19 levels or hit dice or 99 hit points. Those who save only nod and doze, with a 1 in 20 chance per round of waking fully.
  • Fear: by touch only.
  • Summon: 1-4 erinyes (50% chance of success).

Description: much like a satyr, but more human-looking except for his bat-like wings. His skin is pale, his cheeks slightly ruddy.

Devils: general (MMII)

The dwellers and rulers of the planes of Hell are mainly devils, the most powerful of lawful evil creatures. In their traits and abilities they are somewhat like the demons of chaos. Their shared traits are covered here; each type and arch-devil has its own entry, and more is in the MM under “Devil”.

  • Order: devils follow a strict chain of command that they dare not break for fear of the arch-devils. Still, there is great rivalry and open hostility among the devils of the various planes and among the arch-devils. While the lesser devils squabble, the dukes of Hell scheme to seize Asmodeus’s throne, but the archfiend has always played one against another and still rules from his lowest plane.
  • Travel: all devils can move about the planes of Hell (though only the dukes dare do so without authorization), and to Gehenna, Hades, and Acheron at will. They can also move through the Astral Plane, though they seldom do. No devil can enter other planes unless the proper ritual is performed, a gate is opened, or its proper name is spoken (and heard).
  • Death: the material form of a greater devil or duke can be destroyed, but such creatures can only truly be slain if met and fought in Hell or the lower planes next to it. A greater devil whose material form is destroyed is forced into lemure form for 9 decades of torment before it regains its former station. A duke whose material form is destroyed is bound to its own plane of Hell for a decade (unless properly called before the 10 years are up) and suffers a great loss of face.
  • Combat: devils can never be subdued. Lesser ones always fight until destroyed; greater ones will negotiate if seriously threatened. All can direct their attacks at 2 or more opponents if they have the means.
  • Service: devils serve if properly commanded, but it is risky, since an improper command breaks the law that binds them (and it usually takes a contract for the commander’s soul). People other than lawful evil ones can invoke or deal with devils. Properly drawn magic circles (with symbols, for greater and arch-devils) keep devils off for a time. Holy (good) artifacts or relics repel them.
  • Telepathy: a special form lets them understand and converse with any intelligent creature.

  • At will (one at a time, one per round): affect normal fires, change self, command, produce flame, scare, and summon a barbed devil once per day (5% chance of success).
