Giants are huge humanoids. There are 6 major races of giants, described in the MM, plus the minor races listed here and in the FF. Each race has some things in common with the others and many differences; the common traits are in the MM, “Giant”.

system.specialDefenses: Control ground density for 5 foot radius
system.description:
The gibbering mouther is an amoeba-like creature made entirely of mouths and eyes. Its only motive is to eat whatever edible thing is in reach, animal, vegetable, or mineral, so its lair and the land around it are stripped bare. It prefers cold and underground regions.

  • Ambush: its favorite tactic is to wait with eyes and mouths closed, looking like a lump of earth, and surprise a party that stumbles on it.
  • Movement: it oozes forward, fastening several mouths to the ground and pulling itself along. Over fluid, sticky ground such as mud and quicksand it moves faster by muscular contractions, and given the chance it alters the ground (below) to allow this.
  • Armor: its brain is in its middle, and its gelatinous body makes that one vital spot hard to hit, hence armor class 1.
  • Spittle: bursts into a bright flare when it strikes any hard, cold surface. Characters looking at the flash are blinded for 1 round unless they save vs. petrification.
  • Bites: it extends and bites with 6 mouths per round. Each mouth that hits fastens on and drains 1 more point of damage per round. When 3 or more mouths are attached to one character, that person checks each round for slipping: 4 or less on 2d6 means a fall (+1 if dexterity is 15+). The mouther then flows over the fallen victim and bites with 12 more mouths. Once it has pulled down one victim, it will trap other prey if it can.
  • Gibbering: on sighting anything edible it may start an incoherent gibbering that causes confusion in all within 6” unless they save vs. spells; those within range save again each round they hear it. A confused character rolls d8: 1 wanders for 1 round; 2-5 stands stunned for 1 round; 6-7 attacks the nearest living creature for 1 round; 8 runs away for 2 rounds as from a fear spell (save at +2).
  • Altering ground: it always warms the earth and stone within 5 feet of itself, and can change its consistency to a doughy, tarry quicksand or to concrete. Altering earth takes 5 segments; shifting stone to its next nearest form takes 1 full round.

Gloomwings are flying meat-eaters with great speed and agility. Their larval stage is the tenebrous worm (q.v.). Though not as tough as tenebrous worms, they are still deadly, aggressively hunting prey in the air and on the ground.

  • Pattern: the geometric black and silver pattern on its wings and body causes confusion in any intelligent being viewing it squarely from above (save vs. spell). It is also excellent camouflage, making the gloomwing almost impossible to detect, so it surprises on 1-3 on d6.
  • Attacks: creatures on the ground smaller than a halfling are carried off and eaten in midair. Larger prey is attacked by hovering and slashing with its 2 front claws (it lacks the strength and coordination to use all 8) and its mandibles.
  • Pheromone: on the 2nd and each later round of melee it gives off a scent that causes weakness in any non-insect. Those exposed must save vs. poison or lose 1 point of strength per round of exposure, regained 1-4 turns after exposure ends. Those who make the first save need not save again, and several gloomwings do not mean several saves. The scent may also draw 1-4 more gloomwings (20% per round, however many are present).
  • Eggs: egg-laden females (1-2 on d6) lay their eggs in a slain victim’s corpse, which hatch in 12 days into 4-10 tenebrous worms (q.v.). The corpse cannot be resurrected unless the infestation is removed with cure disease, and unless killed, the worms devour the whole body.

Description: huge moths streaked with black and silver over wings and body, with large, fern-like antennae, dusky sable tipped with white. Each of the 8 legs has an iridescent pearl claw, and the extended mouth has a double set of ivory mandibles (worth 25 gp per gloomwing).

Goats live in areas of scrub on hills, plains, and mountains. All attack only if cornered.

  • Charge: bucks may charge, gaining +2 to hit and 1-2 extra points of damage.
  • Herd: 1-2 bucks and up to 12 does, the rest being kids (non-combatants).

Though it looks like a chimera, the gorgimera is a more fearsome monster. This sterile hybrid has the hindquarters and head of a gorgon, the forequarters and head of a lion, and the middle body, wings, and head of a red dragon. Only the lion parts are armor class 5.

  • Attacks: claws, a lion bite, a gorgon butt, and a dragon bite.
  • Breath: the gorgon head breathes petrifying breath twice per day (a cone 3” long, 1” wide at the base); victims turn to stone unless they save vs. petrification. The dragon head breathes fire twice per day (a cone 5” long, 2” wide at the base) for 3-24 (3d8) points of damage, save vs. breath weapon applies.
  • Using breath: knowing breath ranges and effects, it always uses one against opponents 10 feet or more away. In melee, roll d6: 1 dragon breath, 2 gorgon breath, 3-6 normal attacks.
  • Other: it speaks a very limited form of the red dragon language. The gorgon head sees into the Astral and Ethereal Planes, and its breath reaches into them.

Description: almost exactly like a chimera, except that the gorgon parts are metallic blue, with red-rimmed pale blue gorgon eyes.

Green hags are a race of evil creatures related to both annis and night hags (q.v.). Like the annis they live on the Prime Material Plane. Many live in forests and lonely moors, but some live in swamps and rivers; these are often called shellycoats. The lair is always a small cave, perhaps dug in earth.

  • Attacks: claws with rock-hard talons; their 18/00 strength adds +6 to each.
  • Mimicry: to lure victims, they imitate the voice of a man, woman, or child, human or demi-human; calls for help, crying, and so on are common tricks. They can also mimic common animal sounds, such as barnyard fowl, cats, dogs, goats, sheep, and cattle.
  • Spell-like powers (at will, one at a time, one per round, at 9th level): audible glamer, dancing lights, invisibility, pass without trace, change self, speak with monsters, water breathing, weakness.
  • Surprise: their coloring and 90% chance to move silently and hide in foliage (even underwater) let them surprise on 5 in 6 (19 in 20 when attacking from invisibility). Their very keen senses, infravision and ultravision included, mean they are surprised only 1 in 20.
  • Languages: their own (a dialect of Annis), Ogre, common Giant, and Common.

Description: like a night hag with green skin, hair from near-black to olive green, and amber to orange eyes. They often dress as peasants.

system.psionicText: 151 to 250 Attack/Defense Modes: A, C/G, J
system.description:
Grippli look like small, intelligent, humanoid tree frogs. They eat insects and fruit, and their hands and feet are adapted for moving easily through branches. They live 700 years and have few young. They live in swamps and rain forests. They are not warlike, but love bright colors and have been known to raid travelers to steal brightly colored clothing for their huts.

  • Camouflage: gray-green skin, so they surprise on 1-4.
  • Sight: ultravision to 10”, so they do well by night and by day.
  • Weapons: snares, nets, poisoned darts and bolts, and sometimes a sword or dagger.
  • Psionics: a few (1%-2%) are psionic.
  • Lair: mud and wood huts on the ground, with 5-30 males, as many females, and 1-6 non-combatant young. The tribe mother is there too (AC 7; HD 3; damage 1d6+1, and a musk cloud once per day treated as stinking cloud), with 1-3 mates (AC 8; HD 2; damage 1d4+1 + poison).

The leaping grigs seem to be a kind of sprite, found only in sylvan woodlands and meadows. They are shy of strangers but otherwise good-natured and friendly. They are nocturnal and usually met in a glen, where they gather with one or more other bands of grigs, or a tribe of atomies (q.v.), or both, to play and dance in the moonlight; one or more grigs play bowed string instruments while the rest enjoy circle dances and other games.

  • Others present: a 30% chance: on a percentile roll of 01-15, 5-50 grigs; 16-25, 2-12 grigs and 30-120 atomies; 26-30, 5-50 grigs and 30-120 atomies.
  • Armor class: good because of their size, dexterity, and leaping. Their legs are more like a cricket’s or grasshopper’s than a sprite’s, letting them leap long distances, helped by small, gauzy wings.
  • Combat: they attack only evil enemies or those who bother them, usually with missiles then melee. Each carries at least 6 small darts, hurled during their hopping flight at +2 to hit; then they land and thrust with needle-like daggers. In grig hands the darts equal large darts and the daggers do damage as a short sword; in anyone else’s, the darts do only 1 point and the dagger is just a knife.
  • Spell-like powers (at will, one at a time, one per round, at 6th level): change self, entangle, invisibility, pyrotechnics, trip, and ventriloquism. They use them for jolly fun as well as protection, and many practical jokes are reported from meetings with them.
  • Fiddlers: 25% can play a tune equal to the magic-user spell irresistible dance. All within 30 feet save vs. spell or dance until the grig stops or they drop from exhaustion. Grigs can play for hours.
  • Senses: 90% likely to surprise, only 10% likely to be surprised. Hearing twice the human norm, infravision to 180 feet, and ultravision.
  • Languages: their own, Atomie, Brownie, Pixie, and Sprite, and Common if they choose to slow their speech and pitch it lower.

Grim are guardians who watch for and oppose evil. They are night creatures, usually haunting the fringes of human settlements or burial grounds.

  • Forms: a black cat (as a giant lynx, attacks 1-2/1-2/1-4 + raking), a black dog (as a war dog, attack 2-8), or a black owl (as a giant owl, attacks 2-8/2-8/2-5). Each must keep its chosen form for a full night.
  • By day: they become ethereal and wait for sunset; damage taken the day before is healed when the sun sets.
  • Turning: besides their form’s attacks, they turn undead as 8th-level clerics, +2 on the die against evil creatures from the Lower Outer Planes.
  • Defenses: hit only by weapons of +1 or better magic.
  • Protection: each radiates protection from evil in a 10-foot radius and can detect evil at 7”, so evil creatures never surprise them, and their senses let them surprise others 1 in 10.
  • Warnings: they usually ward off evil creatures and warn good folk of danger from such monsters with their weird, mournful yowl, howl, or hoot. They do not otherwise communicate or act with humans or demi-humans unless a confrontation is at hand, in which case they always help fight evil.

system.specialDefenses: +1 or better weapon to hit; immune to earth-based magic
system.description:
(Statistics in parentheses are for the Elemental Plane of Earth, except movement rates.)

The chaggrin, or soil beast, is a grue from the Elemental Plane of Earth. On the Prime Material Plane it usually takes the form of a yellowish hedgehog, though its skull-like head makes it easy to tell from a real one. Only 2 or 3 spans long, it weighs over 140 pounds, some as much as 210.

  • Attack: it loves to torment its victims. It usually digs its long, razor-sharp foreclaws into prey and holds on while the victim runs about trying to escape or dislodge it. Each round of clinging does 7-12 more points of damage, and in hedgehog form its quills do 1-4 points per round to unprotected flesh.
  • Forms: at will a large mole, hedgehog, or two-legged, man-like form (its natural shape on its own plane). In man-like form it can merge into natural soil or stone and emerge suddenly, surprising on 1-5. The only clue is a faint, damp, dark outline, visible only to careful observation.
  • Earth magic: no spell based on or affecting earth works against it, including earthquake, dig, glassee, statue, stone shape, passwall, move earth, glassteel, transmute rock to mud, wall of stone, and stone to flesh. Its mere presence within 40 feet of such magic dispels it, even if it was permanent. Magic items are not affected.

Description: its natural form is disgusting: a body like lumpy, wet clay, an asymmetrical, vicious face, and small eyes gleaming with feral light.

system.specialDefenses: +1 or better weapon to hit; immune to fire-based spells
system.description:
The harginn, or flame horror, is a grue from the Elemental Plane of Fire. Summoned to the Prime Material Plane it usually appears as a human whose lower body and legs are flames. It can also take the shape of a normal bonfire, a column of fire up to about 8 feet high, or a very humanoid bronze statue. It moves fast in any form.

  • Attack: a gout of flame from its fingertips that balloons out over an area 3 feet wide and 6 feet long, damaging all within.
  • Blink: it can blink (as the spell), and always does so in battle.
  • Fire magic: no spell based on or affecting fire works against it, including produce flame, pyrotechnics, produce fire, wall of fire, fire seeds, chariot of sustarre, fire storm, burning hands, fireball, flame strike, flame arrow, fire charm, fire shield, fire trap, delayed blast fireball, incendiary cloud, and meteor swarm. Its presence within 20 feet of such magic dispels it, even if permanent. Magic items are not affected.

Description: truly gruesome; where features can be seen, they show leering evil and great cruelty. Its eyes glow black, and its body has fiery hues such as scarlet and orange, crimson and purple-blue, or yellow and orange.

system.specialDefenses: +2 or better weapon to hit; immune to air-based spells
system.description:
The ildriss, or wind terror, comes from the Elemental Plane of Air. On the Prime Material Plane it is either as invisible as the wind, or seen as a fog-like cloud with vaporous tentacles and 3 faintly gleaming red eyes (its natural form on its own plane).

  • Attack: it whisks about invisibly, but to attack must become more substantial, a misty being. It then whirls, its fog arms carrying small particles that strike with such force they cause horrible scouring wounds, like a storm of wind-driven sand.
  • Surprise: since it can move invisibly high up or along the ground, it always has a 4 in 6 chance of surprise, and it attacks first in any round.
  • Air magic: no spell based on or affecting air works against it, including control weather, wind walk, call lightning, control winds, stinking cloud, gust of wind, lightning bolt, cloudkill, cone of cold, invisible stalker, wall of fog, and fog cloud. If an elemental grue from the Plane of Air is within 50 feet, such spells not only fail but existing effects, even permanent ones, are fully dispelled. Magic items are not affected.
  • Hard to hit: its nebulous, airy form gives it armor class 2. It is less substantial on the Prime Material Plane than other grues, so a +2 or better magic weapon is needed to hit it.

Description: usually gray, pale yellow, or (rarely) white, with pyramid-shaped eyes from dark orange through scarlet to maroon.

system.specialDefenses: +1 or better weapon to hit; immune to water-based spells
system.description:
(Statistics in parentheses are for the Elemental Plane of Water.)

The varrdig, or fluid brute, comes from the Elemental Plane of Water. It can appear as a pool of water, a fountain, or part of a larger body of water, though its greenish tinge tends to give it away to a careful observer. Its real form is a translucent, globular, jelly-like blob with a lower fringe of small clawed legs, and pipe-like tubes radiating from its middle.

  • Water jets: in its own element the tubes jet water to move it; otherwise it attacks with them, the force being considerable out to 6 feet, with a 1 in 6 chance of blinding the victim for 1-4 rounds.
  • Drowning: it drowns a helpless opponent in a single round by thrusting a tube into a nostril.
  • In water: it attacks by rapidly propelling its body into the opponent.
  • Water magic: no spell based on or affecting water works against it or within 30 feet of it; such spells fail, even if previously cast and permanent. These include create water, part water, ice storm, purify food and drink, purify water, wall of ice, create food and water, obscurement, airy water, lower water, and water breathing. Magic items are not affected.
  • Combined form: several varrdigs can join into one being shaped like a snowman, gliding smoothly on their joined legs. The middle part holds the sense organs (if any), shown by odd growths of cilia and stalks, and the top sprouts 3-6 tubes that shoot water streams out to 10 feet for 1-6 hit points of damage.

The hangman tree is named for its rope-like limbs, sinewy vines ending in nooses that, when let down, look much like hanging ropes. These deciduous trees grow in temperate to subtropical lands. Their shallow roots and few leaves force them to add to their nourishment by eating protein directly, so each one traps prey. All are solitary.

  • Movement: very slow: once fully grown, only a few feet per day. Saplings* move about 6 feet per hour, mature trees about a third of that. In freezing weather it puts down a taproot and goes dormant.
  • Treasure: it has no interest in treasure and moves constantly, so treasure is unlikely near one, though indigestible items are expelled from the belly-trunk now and then.
  • Nooses: it drops its nooses around prey. Each tree has 6-9, but can control only 3 at a time. Each takes 13-20 points to sever and destroy, separate from damage to the tree itself. Once in contact, a noose draws tight, doing 1-3 points per round as it lifts the prey (up to 1,000 pounds) to the opening at the top of the trunk, taking 4 full rounds.
  • Digestion: on the 5th round the victim is dropped into the acid in the trunk, taking 3-12 points of acid damage per round until dead, and then is digested. Escape is nearly impossible because of sharp growths around the opening pointing down and inward. About 3 man-sized victims fit at once.
  • Perfume: at will it can release a hallucinatory scent, usually while prey is 30-80 feet away, making victims believe it to be an ordinary quickwood, a treant, etc.
  • Other: it speaks halting Common learned over the years. Drawing power from its surroundings, it has magic resistance based on its age. Lightning or electricity does double damage. Extreme cold shocks it into dormancy until it thaws. Darkness slows it, though it still works at half efficiency.

Description: like a thick oak with few branches and sparse leaves. Knot-like bumps, usually high on the trunk, hold its sense organs, and a scar-like place on the lower trunk is where indigestibles are expelled.

* Optional guide to tree ages: non-combatant sprout, 1-10 years; sapling, 11-25 years; mature tree, 26-75 years; old tree, 76-150 years; ancient tree, 151+ years.
system.hpNote: Printed “61 hp/year”; the book does not explain it further (MMII p.74). Set hit points by hand.

system.description:
(Where statistics are separated by a slash, those on the left are for the haunt in its natural state, those on the right for the haunt inside a possessed victim.)

A haunt is the restless spirit of a person who died leaving a vital task unfinished. It stays within 6” of where it died until it possesses a body, and its only aim is to possess a living body and use it to finish the task, gaining final release. The best defense against a haunt is to leave its area.

  • Forms: at will, a hovering, glowing ball of light (looking exactly like a will-o-wisp), or a hazy, translucent image of its former body. It is often mistaken for a groaning spirit, spectre, or ghost.
  • Dexterity drain: each hit drains 2 points of dexterity, with the penalties of lower dexterity, as a creeping numbness and cold spreads through the body. At zero dexterity the haunt steps into the body and possesses it, and dexterity returns to normal.
  • Possession: it uses the body to finish its task, which need not be dangerous. When done, it passes to its final rest and the victim regains control, with a dexterity of 3, recovering 1 point per turn of complete rest. If the possessed body is slain, the haunt then haunts the place where the body died.
  • Opposed alignment: if the victim’s alignment is opposite to the haunt’s (good vs. evil), it tries to strangle the character: on a successful hit its ghostly hands close on the throat, doing 1 point the first round, 2 the second, 4 the third, and so on, doubling each round until the victim dies or the haunt is driven off.
  • Turning: haunts cannot be turned, being bound to the site of their death.
  • Harming it: in natural form it is struck only by silver and magic weapons, and by fire. Weapons do only 1 point per attack plus magic bonuses; normal fire does 1 point per round, and magical fire full damage. At zero hit points it loses control of its ectoplasm and fades away, re-forming in 1 week to haunt its place again until its task is done. Exorcism destroys it forever.
  • Freeing a victim: attacks on a possessed character do full damage to the character. The only safe ways to free one are exorcism or a hold person spell, against which the haunt must save vs. paralyzation or be driven out.
system.hpNote: Printed “5/victim’s hp”: 5 hit dice in its natural state; when possessing a victim, it uses the victim’s hit points (MMII p.74).

system.description:
Hollyphants are creatures of the Upper Outer Planes, used by the deities as messengers and helpers, so they are sometimes seen on the Prime Material Plane. Usually 1 to 3 are flying; only 5% of the time is one on foot. They travel the Astral and Ethereal Planes in the course of their duties.

  • Aura: a kind of telepathic aura around them fills good characters with great fondness and wish to cooperate, neutral ones with unease, and evil ones with loathing tinged with fear. No saving throw. Hollyphants want to aid good, dislike neutrality, and seek to destroy evil.
  • Attacks: normally with their upward-jutting tusks, but their other powers are far more effective.
  • Trumpeting (3 times per day): blasting as a horn of blasting; deafening as drums of deafening but in a 1” × 3” × 7” cone; or sun-sparkles, a 1” × 2” × 5” cone of positive energy particles doing 8d6+8 points of damage to creatures such as undead and beings of the Lower Outer Planes.
  • Spell-like powers (at will, one at a time, one per round, at 16th level): banish (once per day; see below), bless, cure serious wounds (twice per day), flame strike (once per day), heal (once per day), light, protection from evil 10-foot radius (twice per day), raise dead (once per day), and teleport without error.
  • Banishment: forces a creature from another plane back to its home at once; it cannot return without special summoning or some means of leaving its plane. Several creatures within 2” can be banished if their total hit dice are 32 or less. If a target saves vs. the spell, the hollyphant is stung by a backlash of energy, taking 2-12 points of damage and being stunned for 2-12 segments.
  • Defenses: a living hollyphant’s fur always radiates a globe of invulnerability. Its tusks make it immune to all diseases and poisons (but do not work so for others). It is harmed only by +1 or better magic weapons.
  • Other powers: automatic detect evil in a 2” radius. It can gate (50% success) another hollyphant* (70%) or a suitable deva** (30%). Psionics: usually 4 minor and 2 major disciplines, never duplicating its other powers. It communicates by its own speech or a limited telepathy.

* Alternatively, perhaps a baku, lamassu, opinicus, shedu, etc. ** Alternatively, perhaps a greater lamassu, greater shedu, ki-rin, phoenix, etc.

Description: golden fur that seems to glow, golden wings, small ivory tusks, and large, kindly eyes from amber to glowing brown.

system.specialDefenses: +1 or better weapon to hit, plus see Special Defenses defense Table
system.frequency: Very rare (common on the Planes of Hades)
system.description:
The hordlings of the Hordes of Hades vary in form, size, power, and appearance, but all are hideous and hateful. They roam Hades preying on everything, including each other; the strong kill and eat the weak. They will serve strong leaders such as night hags, but are untrustworthy, rebellious, and quarrelsome, so hordes do not last long (nor do hordlings). Their nature is in fact chaotic. Similar creatures are common in Tarterus, and a few are found in the Abyss. The only known way to bring more than 1 hordling to the Prime Material Plane is the Bringer of Doom, a strange device made by arcane magic during the Invoked Devastation (see the WORLD OF GREYHAWK™ set) and now lost.

system.hpNote: Roll d4 for hit dice (MMII p.75).

system.description:
These small antelope-centaurs look like a cross between a centaur and a pixie, brownie, or sprite. They speak Hybsil, Elf, and Common. Bugbears, ogres, and especially gnolls are their mortal enemies; they are often friendly with most four-legged mammals, including antelopes, zebras, deer, and horses.

  • Weapons: short daggers, but mainly arrows doing 1-4 points of damage, coated with a rare plant juice causing sleep for 1-4 hours (save vs. poison at −4).
  • Hardiness: their hearty constitutions give +4 to all their saving throws.
  • Society: large families or close-knit tribes in temperate or subtropical grasslands. They are semi-nomadic: some roam vast areas, others spend a lifetime in a small thicket or grove. The tribal leader is a witch doctor with druid (60%) or magic-user (40%) spells, up to 7th level.

The jann are the weakest of the elemental humanoids known together as genies (compare dao, djinni, efreeti, marid), because a jann is formed of all 4 elements and so must spend most of its time on the Prime Material Plane.

  • Arms: they often (60%) wear chain mail, giving an effective armor class of 2, and usually use large scimitars (equal to bastard swords) and composite longbows.
  • Strength: males 18/01 to 18/00; females 17 (01-50) to 18/50 (51-00).
  • Powers: besides flying, at will, one at a time, one per melee round: growth and reduction (twice each per day), invisibility (3 times per day), create food and water (once per day, as a 7th-level cleric), and etherealness (once per day, for up to 1 hour). They perform at 12th level unless noted.
  • Elements: they can live in air, earth, fire, or water for up to 48 hours, elemental planes included, and any jann can travel to those planes, taking up to 6 people who hold hands in a circle with it. Not returning to the Prime Material Plane in time does 1 point of damage per hour until it returns or dies. It can travel on to other elemental planes without harm if it spent at least 2 days on the Prime Material Plane just before.

Relations: suspicious of humans; they dislike demi-humans and detest humanoids. They accept djinn but shun dao, efreet, and marids. They prefer forlorn desert areas at hidden oases, for privacy and safety, but sometimes befriend humans or work with them for a reward such as potent magic items.

Society: very open, with males and females equal. A tribe of 11-30 is ruled by a sheik and 1-2 viziers. Exceptionally powerful sheiks are called amirs, and in time of need gather and command large forces of jann (and sometimes allied humans).

  • Leaders: genius intelligence, higher hit dice (printed “up to 84 for sheiks, 95 for amirs”), and greater strength (19 possible 10% of the time).
  • Viziers: genius to supra-genius intelligence and these powers, 3 times per day each at 12th level: augury, detect magic, and divination.
  • Languages: Common, the languages of geniekind, and speech with animals.
system.hpNote: Leaders have higher hit dice, printed “up to 84 for sheiks, 95 for amirs” (MMII p.77).

system.specialDefenses: +1 or better weapon to score effective damage
system.xp: VI/825 + 18/hp (half awarded if half the creature slain)
system.description:
The mustard jelly is a strain or close relative of the ochre jelly, but far more dangerous. The only sign of it is a faint smell like blooming mustard plants; that smell and its see-through yellowish-brown color give it its name.

  • Attack: it forms a pseudopod of its acidic substance and strikes with it.
  • Vapor: it gives off a toxic vapor in a 10-foot radius. Everyone nearby must save vs. poison each round or become lethargic and move at half speed. The effect lasts 2 rounds and is cumulative.
  • Dividing: it can split into 2 smaller, faster halves (move 12-18"), each able to attack, each with half the hit points of the whole. For example, it can flow into a room, split so the halves attack independently and at the same time, then form a ring around a pillar its prey has climbed.
  • Limits: it cannot squeeze through small spaces, and it cannot move along ceilings as an ochre jelly can.
  • Defenses: normal weapons do not harm it. Electrical attacks and magic missiles make it grow, adding hit points equal to the damage rolled. Cold does only half damage; other attacks work normally.

Treasure: it is not unintelligent but does not value treasure. Some may be left over from devoured victims.

The kampfult, also called the sinewy mugger, once lived in thick woodlands, hiding its rope-like body among vines and creepers. It looped its vine-like coils around passing prey and crushed and strangled it. Humans hunted it hard, and the few left are now usually found in ruins or dungeons, where it looks like ropes or a net and surprises the careless.

  • Attack: it can attack several creatures at once. A victim hit by an appendage cannot escape until the kampfult is slain.
  • Harming it: only the central section can be damaged.
  • Body: a trunk about 4 feet long, slightly thicker than the limbs, with 6 attack appendages about 6 feet long and 6 movement appendages 1 foot long spaced along it. It pulls in or holds its appendages to disguise itself.

Keches are evil forest fiends that live to mislead, trap, and eat humans. They roam deep woodlands in every climate from tropical to subarctic, digging pits, setting snares, and rigging deadfalls for travelers. Now and then several small bands join up to raid forest communities and carry victims off somewhere far away to feast in peace. They often imitate cries of distress to lure prey into traps and ambushes.

  • Attack: clawing rakes and a bite.
  • Tactics: they surprise prey 5 in 6, usually rushing 1 or 2 chosen victims, killing them, and carrying off the bodies.
  • Woodcraft: camouflage coloring and skill make it 50% unlikely their tracks can be followed, and they move with a 50% chance of silence.
  • Climbing: long arms and feet with grasping toes let them climb trees very fast (60 feet per round) and swing through the high branches.

Description: green humanoids covered in leathery, leaf-like skin, with human-like faces, large mouths full of fangs, and jutting jaws.

These dance-loving folk always carry cudgels and large pouches holding hair, shears, and other items.

  • Hair snares: they can trap intruders by weaving the hair into animated, entangling ropes and snares in 1-4 rounds (rope: AC I (as printed); hp 5; MV 3"; save vs. paralysis or be trapped).
  • Pouch: the items in a korred’s pouch turn to gold (worth 50-200 gp) if sprinkled with holy water.
  • Strength: korreds are very strong and can hurl boulders up to 10" (damage 2d8). They are said to have built the druid stone circles.
  • Weapons: shears (damage d4+4), cudgel (damage d6+4), or bare-handed (damage 1-2+4).
  • Laughter (3 times per day): anyone within 6" who hears it must roll their charisma or higher on 1d20 or be stunned for 1-4 rounds.
  • At will: stone shape, animate rock, stone door (teleport 3"), shatter rock, transmute rock to mud, and stone tell.
  • Weekly dance: each week they hold a holiday of dancing and music. Anyone who interrupts must save vs. spells or join the dance, losing 1-4 points per round until dead, restrained, or the korreds flee.

Kraken are a race of squid-like creatures that breathe both air and water and live in the dark depths of the ocean. Legend says they were once smaller, lived in shallow coastal waters, and had human worshippers who served them and brought them sacrifices. Some upheaval in nature, and perhaps a battle with forces of Good, drove the survivors into the depths. Their numbers shrank to a handful, but those few grew huge and powerful. They now seek to kill every good creature and devour all small life. They are aggressive hunters who will fight even large sperm whales, and usually win.

  • Armor: tentacles and the exposed head are AC 6; the body has a very thick, tough shell and is AC 0.
  • Movement: jetting backward at 21"; swimming at 3".
  • Attacks: 2 barb-covered tentacles, 4-6 other striking tentacles, and possibly a bite from its huge beak. At least 2 of its 10 tentacles are used to anchor or steady it. The barbed tentacles rake and pull prey to the beak.
  • Constriction: the other tentacles, if they hit, wrap and squeeze, doing 3-12 points of damage on the 2nd and each later round. To escape, the tentacle must be cut off (16 points of damage from sharp weapons). See "Squid, Giant" for how tentacle hits hinder victims.
  • Escape with prey: if 4 or more tentacles hold prey while the kraken is taking damage, it slips away to the depths with its victims, to its den in an undersea cavern at least 1000 feet below the surface.
  • Retreat: if 3 or more of its tentacles are cut off, it retreats at once.
  • Ink: its ink cloud is 8" × 8" × 12" long and stays poisonous for 2-5 rounds until the water dilutes it. Creatures inside take 1-4 points of damage per round, while the kraken jets backward to its lair.

Attacking ships: a kraken attacks ships to drag them down. It is at least 10% larger than the largest giant squid and can pull vessels 60 feet long under the water. Larger ships are dragged to a halt in 10 rounds. If it keeps a constricting grip with 6 or more tentacles for 3 rounds in a row, the ship takes damage as if rammed. It then takes on water, and within 2-8 rounds it can be dragged under because it has lost buoyancy.

Innate powers: airy water in a sphere (128 feet across) or a hemisphere 6 times as large as usual (240 feet across), lasting a full day. It can also use these spell-like powers, one at a time, at will:

  • faerie fire for 8 hours;
  • control temperature within a 40-foot radius for 1 day;
  • control winds once per day;
  • weather summoning once per day;
  • animal (fish) summoning III 3 times per day (this brings fish to the area but does not control them).

Lairs: some kraken are said to keep cavern complexes where they hold and breed human slaves to serve and feed them. They stock these undersea dungeons by using wind and weather to bring ships to the area. Such lairs are 50% likely to hold treasure type A as well as the treasure listed.

Like their smaller, weaker kin, greater lammasu prefer warm regions but sometimes go even into arctic ones. They also protect and help good creatures, especially lawful ones, and usually live with 6 or more ordinary lammasu.

  • Travel: they can travel the Astral and Ethereal Planes at will.
  • At will (one at a time, 1 per round): become invisible, dimension door, and teleport without error.
  • Protection: they radiate protection from evil in a 20-foot radius with double effect: −4 to evil attacks and +4 on any saving throws.
  • Clerical spells (5th level ability): 5 1st-level, 4 2nd-level, 3 3rd-level, 2 4th-level, and 1 5th-level spells.
  • Cures: double strength, based on 1d6+1, so cure light wounds heals 4-14 lost hit points and cure serious wounds has double effect (8-28).
  • Holy word: fifty percent can also speak a holy word.
  • Level: their spell-like abilities work at level 12 (as hit dice).
  • Communication: empathy and telepathic communication; they speak the limited language of lawful good and the lammasu tongue.

The land lamprey is a mutated sea lamprey that breathes air and moves like a snake. It lives in almost any climate except desert or extreme cold, preferring dark, damp places.

  • Feeding: like its sea cousins, it bites, fastens on with its round sucking mouth, and drains blood. Attaching is a hit for 1 point of damage; it then drains blood for 3 rounds in a row (unless killed or removed first) for 1 hit point of damage per round.
  • Encumbrance: each lamprey attached to a character encumbers them, equal to losing 1 point of dexterity per lamprey.
  • Removal: only by killing them or exposing them to fire, which makes them let go to avoid the flames.

Description: only about 3 feet long, but fairly thick and heavy, colored light green to blackish green.

The luck eater looks like a golden-furred cat. It can be found almost anywhere, often lurking in a hidden niche, and surprises on 1-4.

  • Purr: when approached it purrs. All creatures within 30 feet must save vs. spell or become attracted to it, wanting to take it along unharmed. It always allows this and stays with its victim(s) for 2-5 hours, purring the whole time. A successful save has no effect, but everyone in range must save each round until attracted.
  • Aura: all creatures within range of the purr suffer a 10% (−2) penalty on all saving throws, damage, and chances to hit. The luck eater somehow feeds on the luck lost this way and is full only once the time above has passed.
  • Hunger: if it goes 3 turns without food (no rolls made in 30 minutes of character time), it changes its purr slightly, making its keepers attack the next creature they meet. If another 3 turns pass without food, it changes the aura again so its keepers fight each other for 10 rounds or until someone dies. This ends the enchantment, and the luck eater always slips away unnoticed near the end of the fight.
  • Leaving: otherwise it leaves quickly once full, still purring. Those it attracted let it go, defending it if needed, and come to their senses 1-6 turns later.

system.specialDefenses: Hit only by silver or +1 or better magic weapons
system.description:
Foxwomen are lycanthropes with 3 forms instead of the usual 2; the statistics above give all 3. They have infravision (6") in every form. They avoid others of their own kind and live in lonely woodlands, in a hidden cottage or comfortable cave complex with all the usual human comforts.

Companions: a foxwoman always has 2-5 charmed males as servants and companions, armed and doing their utmost to protect her. They may be elven (25%), human (25%), or half-elven (50%).

  • At least 1 is a fighter (70%) or ranger (30%) of 2nd-5th level.
  • There is a 50% chance for any 1 of the others to also be a fighter of 1st-4th level.
  • There is a 10% chance that 1 of the remaining males is a 1st-4th level cleric (10%), druid (45%), magic-user (5%), illusionist (5%), thief (25%), or other class (10%).
  • An elf or half-elf may be multi-classed (25% chance for 2 or 3 professions), and is automatically so if the rolls above call for "doubling up".
  • All other males are 0-level fighters, and 1-hit die elves and half-elves.
  • Find the males’ magic items with Appendix P in the DUNGEON MASTER’S GUIDE.

Stolen child: there is a 10% chance she has stolen an elven girl, infected her, and is raising her as a foxwoman. The child is 6-13 (1d8+4) years old; at 12 or 13 treat her as a normal foxwoman, otherwise she does not fight. Foxwomen can pass on lycanthropy only in vixen form.

Silver fox form: she looks like nothing more than a large fox. She moves very fast (24"), can pass without trace (as the spell), and is 90% undetectable in natural cover if she gets out of sight for only 1 segment.

Vixen form: a mix of fox and elf: a silver-furred elf with a fox-like head. Her fierce bite infects elven and half-elven females, who become foxwomen within 3 days unless both cure disease and remove curse are used.

Elven woman form:

  • Comeliness: 21 with respect to human and demi-human males. Males of wisdom 13 or less are in effect under a charm spell; those of 14 or more are not charmed but still find her attractive.
  • Captives: preferred males are kept; others are quietly slain. Dwarves, gnomes, and halflings are always slain when the chance comes.
  • Magic: she uses magic at a level between 1st and 4th, but cannot advance. Roll her cantrips and spells known (and in spell books) randomly.
  • Elven traits: 90% resistant to sleep and charm spells, and +1 with bow and sword (as a normal elf).
  • Tell-tale: her hair is silver or silver-streaked with a widow’s peak, which can warn a careful person that she is a foxwoman.

Lycanthropes: general (MMII)

Lycanthropes are humans who can take animal form. They most often change to animal form during the hours of darkness, and when the moon is full they are 90% likely to be forced into it. They usually go about as humans for whatever purposes they have. Each kind knows its own language as well as Common.

Infection: any humanoid bitten by a lycanthrope for damage equal to 50% or more of its total hit points (but not actually killed and eaten) catches lycanthropy.

  • Belladonna: if the victim carries belladonna and eats it within 1 hour, there is a 25% chance it cures the affliction. It incapacitates the victim for 1-4 days, and there is a 1% chance its poison kills.
  • Cure disease: otherwise, a cure disease spell from a patriarch of 12th or higher level must be cast on the victim within 3 days, or he or she becomes a lycanthrope in 7-14 days.

Some other kinds of lycanthrope exist, but they are extremely rare.

system.specialDefenses: Hit only by silver, cold iron, or +1 or better magic weapons
system.description:
Seawolves suffer from a most evil form of lycanthropy. They roam the waters in packs, hunting and seeking ships to attack so they can pass on their curse. Most were once fishermen or sailors.

  • Boarding: on sighting a ship they follow it, slip aboard in human form, and attack. Usually 1 or 2 deckhands are bitten to death and their weapons taken, and then the general assault begins.
  • Weapons that harm them: iron weapons, as well as silver and magic ones.
  • Infection: a non-fatal bite causes seawolf lycanthropy in 2-5 days. The victim then throws himself or herself overboard at night, changes to seawolf form, and swims off to find a pack.
  • Breathing: they breathe air. They can stay under for 17-24 minutes but must surface for air.

Description: in human form, a wolf-like face, tiny ears, and thick fur all over, the head hair flowing down the neck and shoulders in a mane. In seawolf form, a huge, wolf-headed seal with a mouth full of fangs.

Lycanthropes: general (MMII)

Lycanthropes are humans who can take animal form. They most often change to animal form during the hours of darkness, and when the moon is full they are 90% likely to be forced into it. They usually go about as humans for whatever purposes they have. Each kind knows its own language as well as Common.

Infection: any humanoid bitten by a lycanthrope for damage equal to 50% or more of its total hit points (but not actually killed and eaten) catches lycanthropy.

  • Belladonna: if the victim carries belladonna and eats it within 1 hour, there is a 25% chance it cures the affliction. It incapacitates the victim for 1-4 days, and there is a 1% chance its poison kills.
  • Cure disease: otherwise, a cure disease spell from a patriarch of 12th or higher level must be cast on the victim within 3 days, or he or she becomes a lycanthrope in 7-14 days.

Some other kinds of lycanthrope exist, but they are extremely rare.

These savage lycanthropes have 2 forms:

  • Seawolf: a furred, porpoise-shaped mammal with a wolf’s head. In this form packs hunt sea creatures, surrounding prey and biting with their canine fangs.
  • Wolfman: a man-shape with the fur, claws, and teeth of a seawolf. Its statistics are in parentheses above.
  • Breathing: they breathe air and must surface now and then, holding their breath as dolphins do.
  • Weapons: unlike other lycanthropes, they can be hit by normal weapons.
  • Infection: humans who take 50% or more damage from seawolves catch this lycanthropy. Infected on land, they travel to the sea as fast as they can; at sea, they vanish overboard at the next full moon.
  • Ships: a pack that meets a ship changes to wolfman form and tries to board it, with the sole aim of killing everyone aboard and sinking the ship.

Some other kinds of lycanthrope exist, but they are extremely rare.

system.specialDefenses: Hit only by silver or +1 or better magic weapon
system.description:
Weresharks are humans with a lycanthropy that lets them take shark form whenever they choose, as long as it is dark. They are found only in tropical areas.

  • Human form: almost impossible to tell from a normal human, though large, muscular, cruel, and domineering.
  • Shark form: huge, looking like a great white shark.
  • Habits: solitary; they will readily attack and eat true sharks if the mood takes them.
  • Lair: some set up an underwater lair where sunken treasure lies, guarding it for use in human form. It may be a few hundred coins or a large hoard (such as type F). The lair is always guarded by 2-5 normal sharks, whether or not the wereshark is there.

Lycanthropes: general (MMII)

Lycanthropes are humans who can take animal form. They most often change to animal form during the hours of darkness, and when the moon is full they are 90% likely to be forced into it. They usually go about as humans for whatever purposes they have. Each kind knows its own language as well as Common.

Infection: any humanoid bitten by a lycanthrope for damage equal to 50% or more of its total hit points (but not actually killed and eaten) catches lycanthropy.

  • Belladonna: if the victim carries belladonna and eats it within 1 hour, there is a 25% chance it cures the affliction. It incapacitates the victim for 1-4 days, and there is a 1% chance its poison kills.
  • Cure disease: otherwise, a cure disease spell from a patriarch of 12th or higher level must be cast on the victim within 3 days, or he or she becomes a lycanthrope in 7-14 days.

Some other kinds of lycanthrope exist, but they are extremely rare.

system.specialDefenses: +1 or better weapon to hit; immune to fire-based attacks
system.description:
Magmen come from the Para-elemental Plane of Heat (see the DEITIES & DEMIGODS™ Cyclopedia). Now and then they pass to the Prime Material Plane through gaps made by the great pressure and heat of underground lava. Molten rock here has a different "taste" from that on their own plane, and they like to visit to absorb its essences. They especially like swimming in active volcanoes, because an eruption lets them out to enjoy their favorite sport: setting fire to everything that will burn. They are not very smart, but they are mischievous and love watching Prime Material creatures flee from flames they themselves think harmless; it never occurs to them that others might really be hurt.

  • Combustion touch: they are not really interested in fighting, but try to set any creature they meet on fire for fun. A hit ignites all the creature’s flammable items, burning for 1-8 points of damage per round for 3-6 (1d4+2) rounds, plus any extra damage from flammables carried, such as flasks of oil. Combustible magic items such as scrolls get a save vs. normal fire.
  • When hurt: a magman that is actually hurt runs away, but if cornered it defends itself with a molten fist for 3-24 points of damage. Fire-resistant creatures, including those magically protected, take only half damage.
  • Defenses: a +1 or better weapon is needed to hit one, but any weapon of less than +2 that touches it melts. They are immune to all fire-based attacks.
  • Out of lava: they can stay out of lava only 6 hours before they stiffen and cannot move. They rarely stay out more than 2 or 3 hours, since they think anything under 1000 degrees is cold.
  • Languages: none of the Prime Material Plane.

Description: glowing, man-shaped creatures 3 feet tall, with small puffs of flame bursting constantly from their skin. Each gives off heat like a small bonfire, making the area near it quite uncomfortable.

A mandragora is a plant creature that lurks in woodlands and preys on unwary humans. A group usually lairs in the heavy soil of a forest, preferring spots near ipp trees, briar, or willows. They dig a network of narrow burrows so they can attach to tree roots and feed when no human food is available. They are creatures of darkness: if a lair is opened to full daylight, they are stunned by the light for 1-4 segments.

  • Attack: they whip with their tentacle-like upper limbs, causing cuts, and can strangle a victim struck around the throat.
  • Strangling: any to-hit roll of 20 is a neck/throat hit, which then does 1-4 points of strangling damage per round and reduces the mandragora to 1 attack. If the other upper limb also hits on a 20, strangling damage is doubled and it makes no other attacks besides choking. The strangling continues until the mandragora is killed.
  • Plant nature: spells that normally affect animals do not affect it, and sleep has no effect. Because it is always wet and slimy, it takes only half damage from all fire.
  • Senses: its small, hair-like roots let it "smell" and "hear". It always senses creatures within 120 feet, but will not leave its lair to attack until the sun sets.

Description: a mottled brown and black covering that oozes greenish fluid. Its splayed root-legs, trunk, upper limbs, and pointed "head" with warty growths like a human face make it look man-like. It is often confused with the mandrake, an entirely different creature.

The towering giant mantis lives only where plants grow large enough to hide it, its green color and shape blending in while it waits for prey. It prefers to eat giant insects of various kinds, but attacks any creature it sees as alive and edible.

  • Forelimbs: 2 vise-like forelimbs. A hit does 2-12 points of damage and holds prey with less than 19 strength.
  • Bite: the next round it bites with its sharp, tearing mandibles for 3-12 points of damage. Held prey gets no dexterity or shield bonus.
  • Surprise: it is 75% likely to attack by surprise.
  • Hiding: if it sees another creature as dangerous, it keeps still and avoids being noticed 75% of the time.

This plant lures prey by scent, traps it, and dissolves it in acid.

  • Pollen: during daylight it gives off pollen all the time. Every creature within 60 feet must save vs. poison or become fascinated by the smell.
  • Leaf traps: fascinated creatures go to the plant and even climb willingly into 1 of its 2-5 leaf traps, which close tight around them.
  • Acid: the victim takes damage each round equal to its armor class (ignoring dexterity bonuses; minimum 1 point per round). Items in the acid must save once per turn; all metal gets +2.
  • Escape: victims cannot be pulled free until the plant is dead. The fascination cannot be ended until the smell sours 24 hours later, unless the plant is burned.

A margoyle is an especially horrid kind of gargoyle, found mostly in natural caves and caverns.

  • Camouflage: its body is so much like stone that it is 80% likely to go unnoticed when lurking against stone, so it can often surprise opponents.
  • Attacks: 2 claws, a pair of horns, and a bite with stony fangs.
  • Defenses: only magic weapons of +1 or better harm it.
  • Treasure: despite its low intelligence it gathers valuable items, especially magic ones that could harm it.
  • Language: similar to that of gargoyles, and it speaks the gargoyle tongue well enough.
  • Company: sometimes (20%) found with its lesser kin, gargoyles, as their master or leader.

The marid is the most powerful of all geniekind (see "Dao", "Djinni", "Efreeti", and "Jann"). Marids are formed of material from the Elemental Plane of Water. They are rare even on their own plane and seldom come to the Prime Material Plane.

  • Twice each per day (one at a time): detect evil/good, detect invisible, detect magic, become invisible, assume liquid form (like assume gaseous form), polymorph self, purify water.
  • Up to 7 times per day: assume gaseous form, lower water, part water, create a wall of fog, and give water breathing to others for up to 1 full day.
  • Always: create water, which they can shoot in a powerful jet up to 6" long that both blinds the one struck (saving throw applies) and does 1-6 points of damage; and water walk (as the ring).
  • Once per year: alter reality.
  • Spell level: they perform at 26th level.
  • Carrying: a marid can carry 10,000 gp of weight freely. Double that tires it in only 3 turns; for every 2000 gp under 20,000, add 1 turn (as printed, 12,000 gp can be carried for 8 turns before it tires). A tired marid must rest for 6 turns.
  • Water: they swim very fast, breathe water, and are at home at any depth. They have both ultravision and infravision.
  • Resistances: water-based spells do not harm them. Against cold-based spells they get +2 on saving throws and −2 on each die of damage. Fire does +1 per die of damage, with saving throws at −1. Steam does not harm them.

Society: they tolerate djinn without much liking them, and the same goes for jann; dao and efreet they dislike. They are loosely ruled by a padisha, since every marid claims to be at least a shah, atabeg, beglerbeg, or mufti. The race is very independent and self-centered. Forcing a marid to serve is very hard; bribery and flattery work slightly better, but a marid can never be relied on. They speak all languages through a form of ESP, and the Astral, Elemental, Ethereal, and Prime Material Planes are all open to them.

These hound-like creatures normally live on the Plane of Shadow, where they roam in packs or are used as trained guard beasts.

  • In shadow (the Plane of Shadow, moonlight, etc.): a terrible foe. It can strike and then blend into the shadows so it is 40% unlikely to be seen.
  • In bright light: it loses 50% of its normal movement and cannot hide in shadows.
  • Baying: a pack’s baying always causes panic unless a save vs. spells is made: the victim flees directly away from the sound, dropping anything held. For each number of mastiffs under 10, add +1 to the roll (a 1 always fails); for every 2 mastiffs over 12, subtract 1 (as printed).
  • Whelps: a pack’s lair is 50% likely to hold 2-5 whelps, which can be taken and sold for 200-500 gp each.
system.hpNote: −1 hit point per die in bright light (MMII p.84).

system.description:
Mihstu are free-willed elementals that normally live on the Para-elemental Plane of Air, but are sometimes found in cool, damp places with little or no sunlight. They look like clouds of swirling mist and can seep through small cracks and openings.

  • Attack: they shape their bodies at will; to attack they form 4 solid tentacles tipped with razor-sharp talons.
  • Envelop: a mihstu can wrap a victim in its misty body and drain 1 constitution point per round. At 0 constitution the victim dies. One point returns per full day of rest, and during that time wounds can be healed only by magic.
  • Defenses: harmed only by +2 or better weapons; immune to all electrical and missile attacks (even magic missile). Cold-based attacks only stun them for 2d6 rounds.
  • Habits: solitary, they prefer to be left alone and take a ghostly shape to scare intruders away. They may do tasks for powerful magic-users in return for large payments of powerful magic items.

The miner is a relative of the trapper adapted to life in the woods. It is a carnivore that eats small woodland animals, but it often uses an ambush to get bigger meals.

  • Ambush: it tunnels through earth to lie a few inches under a path or road, then pushes the tips of its spinal barbs up through the surface. The barbs look like twigs, so passing creatures usually do not notice them and may step on them (75% chance if surprised, otherwise 25% per creature passing).
  • Spotting: an unsurprised druid or ranger has a 5% chance per level to see and correctly identify the barbs.
  • Poison: anyone stepping on a barb must save vs. poison or be paralyzed for 2-40 turns.
  • Attack: it waits until all movement above has stopped, then digs out and attacks what it caught, enveloping it just as a trapper (q.v.) does. It also attacks this way if engaged in combat.
  • Hard to reach: it usually stays underground while hunting, so it is hard to attack unless dug out.

Description: less shapeless than a trapper, it usually looks like a tailless ray. Its skin is mottled brown or greenish brown. Its front edge is hard bone, running back to a central ridge on its back lined with 6-25 brown barbs.

system.hd: See below; roughly 1/4 of full size
system.move: As full size multiplied by 2/3, rounded up
system.attacks: As full size or fewer (itemized below)

system.description:
Minimals (short for "miniature animals") are small mammals. They were (and perhaps still are) made with spells like those that so successfully created giant reptiles, insects, amphibians, and the like.

  • Where found: in a place where they live (an isolated valley, small island, or peninsula) they are 80% likely to be the only kind of mammal around. They are seldom if ever found where large carnivores live, which would soon wipe them out. They are sometimes found with brownies, pixies, dryads, leprechauns, etc. (30% likely if the encounter is in a truly isolated place).
  • Behavior: they match their full-sized cousins in most ways, but herd together more often, are more aggressive, and lean strongly toward chaos. Carnivorous minimals are more aggressive than their full-sized kin. They respect larger opponents and usually attack only small prey or when they have greater numbers, though they fight if cornered.
  • Frequency: any kind is 50% likely to be more common than the full-sized animal (as given in the MM or the FF).
  • Size effects: their armor class is 2 places worse and their movement is cut by ⅓ (always rounded up in their favor). Hit dice range from as low as ¼ to as high as 3+4.
  • Surprise: being small, they are more likely to surprise and less likely to be surprised.
  • Damage: never more than 3-6 points from any one attack, and most special attacks are lost.
  • Saving throws: being made by magic, they get +2 on all saving throws and use the full-sized animal’s saving throw vs. death and poison. They get +4 against any spell that would charm them, including the druid spell animal friendship.
  • Familiars: minimals cannot and will not be familiars under any circumstances.

system.description:
Monodrones make up most of Nirvana’s population. They are single-function modrons, usually given some simple labor, or serving as a group to form the regiments of the Nirvanan Army. Thousands of spherical monodrones armed with spears, fauchards, and crossbows make an impressive sight against a foe, as does their unswerving, single-minded performance. They exist for their work, and what little conversation they can manage is usually about their tasks.

  • Units: usually groups of 12, supervised by a duodrone or tridrone.
  • Messengers: one twelfth of all monodrones lack the spider-like arms and instead have fan-like wings joined to the body at one point. These faster, smaller ones serve as messengers and can relay any message of up to 48 words perfectly. Unlike their armed kin, messengers cannot survive in liquid surroundings.
  • Senses: slightly below a normal human’s, with limited infravision (30-foot range).

Modrons: general (MMII)

The Plane of Nirvana is a plane of balance and absolute order: equally hot and cold, equally light and dark, and made of equal parts solid and liquid. Its chief inhabitants are the modrons, who live in a rigid caste system under the absolute rule of Primus the One.

The great wheel: Nirvana is laid out like a great wheel with the Tower of Primus at the hub. The wheel is infinitely wide but divided into 64 sectors, each with its own governor. Four sectors make a region, kept by its ruler; 4 regions make a quarter, ruled by a viceroy; and the 4 quarters are ruled by Primus. The wheel can be reached by astral means or by portals connecting to Arcadia, Acheron, and the Plane of Concordant Opposition, but the portals move as the wheel turns around the Tower of Primus.

Society: all beings are classified, all actions regulated, and all procedures spelled out. Laws are obeyed at once and without question. The base modrons are the most numerous and serve as the working class; the hierarch modrons are the leaders, enforcers, and governors. The castes are:

CasteNumberRole
Base modrons
Monodrones300 million +General laborers
Duodrones55 million +Complex tasks
Tridrones6 million +Multiple tasks, minor supervision
Quadrones1.5 million +Multiple complex tasks, supervision
Pentadrones500 thousand +Lesser police, law enforcement
Hierarch modrons
Decatons100Physical welfare of the base modrons
Nonatons81Police supervision
Octons64Governors of the sectors of Nirvana
Septons49Inspectors
Hextons36Generals of the armies of Nirvana
Quintons25Bureau chiefs and record-keepers
Quartons16Rulers of the regions of Nirvana
Tertians9Judges
Secundi4Viceroys of the 4 quarters
Primus(The One)Absolute ruler of Nirvana

Chain of command: a modron always checks with its superior when facing something beyond its expertise or covered by the regulations. If the superior does not know, the question goes on up the chain. Most base modron questions stop at a pentadrone or decaton; questions about regulations sometimes reach the quintons, and a precious few reach the tertians.

  • Immunities: modrons are not affected by illusions or magic that affects the mind (beguilement, charm, domination, hold, hypnosis, and sleep, for example). Fear and other emotion spells have no effect, nor do attacks based on the Positive or Negative Planes (including life-draining or life-stealing).
  • Resistances: all modrons save vs. cold, fire, and acid at +1 and take −1 per die of damage from them.
  • Hierarchs: the upper tier are never surprised, and their precise order lets them decide the initiative order in a melee round. Each hierarch also has these spell-like powers, at will, one per melee round: clairaudience, clairvoyance, command, dimension door, teleport without error, and wall of force. They can travel the Astral and Ethereal Planes but never do so unless Primus commands it.
  • Language: modrons speak their own precise, complex tongue, from which lawful neutral speech comes. All hierarchs can also communicate telepathically, to a distance set by rank:
RankMiles
Decaton44
Nonaton63
Octon80
Septon190
Hexton216
Quinton238
Quarton384
Tertian405
Secundi420
PrimusAll Nirvana

Death and promotion: base modrons slain anywhere return to the energy pool of Nirvana and re-form as new modrons in 9 days. When there are too many, lower ranks are promoted and the top tier, the pentadrones, is thinned out: infirm or damaged pentadrones go to the pool for good. Hierarchs slain in Nirvana also join the energy pool and are reborn in 9 days. Those slain elsewhere return straight to Primus and are not reborn; the gap is filled by promoting a lower hierarch 1 step, and so on down the line until an outstanding pentadrone is promoted to the hierarchy as a decaton. Promotion takes 1 day, during which the modron changes shape into its new form and does nothing else.

Any hierarch higher than the one involved can promote it, or demote it, sending the offender back to the energy pool to be rebuilt later. While Primus lives, the hierarch ranks stay fairly constant. If Primus is slain, the 4 secundi compete for a week to slay as many powerful chaotic creatures (counted in levels) as possible. The slayers of Primus are judged chaotic at once and count as 100 times their level. The winning secundus receives the spirit of Primus and becomes the new One and Prime, master of Nirvana.

Rogue units: there is a very small chance that modrons met are defective, through natural decay or exposure to outside, chaotic forces. This is most common among base modrons; a few hierarchs have been affected, but never one of quarton rank or higher. Rogues do not follow Primus’ wishes and orders; they break laws, disobey, and may turn violent. They are usually hunted down by the efficient pentadrone police under the nonatons.

The armies of Nirvana: there are 36 great armies, each a powerful fighting force. Each of the 16 regions has its own army, and the secundi have 2 armies each besides their regional forces. The tertians have 3 armies to help with law enforcement and punishment. The last 9 serve Primus directly: 1 as the official tower guard and 8 to be sent out as needed.

  • Army: commanded by a hexton; 4 corps, each led by 40 pentadrones in telepathic contact with the hexton.
  • Corps: 2 divisions, each commanded by 20 pentadrones.
  • Division: 4 brigades, each led by 10 pentadrones. A brigade has 70 officers, 192 NCOs, 252 messengers, and 2628 line troops, 3142 in all.
  • Brigade: 4 regiments. The regiment is the standard tactical unit, led by 5 pentadrones.
  • Regiment: 2 "battles", a squad of winged monodrone messengers, and a special squad of 12 pentadrones.
  • Battle: led by 4 quadrones; 6 companies of monodrones, 2 companies of duodrones, a special company of tridrones, a squad of quadrones, and another squad of messengers.
  • Company: the 8 regular companies are each split into 2 wings plus a headquarters unit. Each company has 12 squads and 3 officers.
  • Squad: 12 troops, including an NCO of the same type as the troops.
  • Special units: messengers, "shock troops", and the like may be attached to the headquarters units of brigades, divisions, and corps.

system.description:
Duodrones are two-function modrons that can supervise 12 monodrones or do complex tasks beyond a monodrone’s abilities. In the forces of Nirvana they serve as noncommissioned officers and as special shock troops armed with thrusting and smashing weapons.

  • Nature: blocky and rectangular, very strong, and completely obedient to their superiors.
  • Speech: limited conversation, but they report their work and observations clearly and completely.
  • Senses: equal to most humans’, with normal-range infravision (90 feet).

system.description:
Tridrones look like 3-sided pyramids with spidery arms and legs. Their main job is supervising lower modrons.

  • Duties: they oversee gross units of 144 monodrones and duodrones, work on multi-task projects, and lead companies in the regiments of the Army of Nirvana.
  • Javelins: guard units and special companies of tridrones carry 3 javelins each, thrown before entering melee.
  • Thinking: they can report actions and observations and even plan limited objectives on the battlefield.
  • Senses: equal to a human’s, with infravision (90 feet) and ultravision (100 yards).

system.description:
The cube-shaped quadrones are the top level of workers in Nirvana. They have 4 complete functions, most of them not tied to carrying out some task. They also serve as field officers in the regiments of Nirvana, and each battle has a special "dozen-unit" of the best quadrone fighters.

  • Archery: excellent archers, able to use 2 bows at the same time.
  • Thinking: they can report actions and observations, make plans, react to the unexpected, and act to fix it.
  • Winged quadrones: some have wings in place of 1 set of arms, so they cannot use bows. They are used for special missions or air combat.
  • Senses: 150% of human normal, with infravision (180-foot range) and ultravision (200-yard range). With sense organs on all 6 sides, they are never surprised under normal circumstances.

system.description:
Each of the 64 octons governs a sector of Nirvana. The sector’s base modrons, and the decatons and nonatons assigned to the governor, are its wards and responsibility. Octons guard their sectors very strictly, making sure regulations are obeyed, routine kept, and reports always correct.

  • Movement: a round collar at shoulder level, part of its body, forces air or liquid through it, giving lift, propulsion, and great maneuverability in air and water. Its 8 tentacle-arms are attached to the outside of the collar.
  • Spells: as 14th-level clerics.
  • At will (once per round, one at a time): water walking as the ring, haste, detection of good/evil, and telekinese 3500 gp weight.
  • Psionics: totally immune to psionic combat and psionic effects.
  • Staff: 1 decaton, 1 nonaton, 5 pentadrones, 16 quadrones, 81 tridrones, 256 duodrones, and 1728 monodrones. Octons keep small towers, smaller versions of those of the quartons, the secundi, and Primus.

Russet mold grows only in damp places underground. At more than 30 feet away it is often mistaken for rust (70% chance).

  • Immunities: weapons, fire, and cold do not harm it.
  • Weaknesses: alcohol, acid, and things harmful to plants (such as salt). A cure disease or continual light cast on it kills it instantly.
  • Spores: it makes no physical attacks, but gives off a barely visible cloud of spores in a 3-foot radius (beyond that the spores settle, harmless), and injects spores if touched. Anyone passing within 3 feet or touching it takes 5-20 points of damage and must save vs. poison; failure brings a sickness that kills in 2-5 turns unless cure disease is cast.
  • Transformation: a character killed by touching it sprouts mold from the spores left by the contact. When the body is fully covered, a vegepygmy (q.v.) rises from the remains. This takes 21-24 hours (1d4+20). A hold plant spell stops the growth for its duration. Once the mold has grown for more than 1 hour, only a wish can recover the victim.

Description: golden-brown to rust-red, lumpy like cold porridge, and covered in short, hair-like growths that stand upright and sway constantly as if in a gentle breeze.

hpOptions.label: 12-16 hit points for each 10 square feet

system.hpNote: Printed “12-16 hp/10 square feet”: roll once per 10 square feet of mold and add them up.

system.description:
Mongrelmen are not a race of their own, but they do not clearly belong to any other. Each is a mixture of many creatures and may carry the blood of humans, orcs, gnolls, ogres, dwarves, hobgoblins, bugbears, elves, bullywugs, and others. For this reason they are rarely welcome in lawful or good societies and are usually abused or enslaved by chaotic and evil ones, which has forced them to learn special survival skills.

  • Camouflage: they hide themselves and their belongings with great skill. Camouflaging himself, another creature, or an item normally takes 1 turn. The chance of going unnoticed is 80%, plus 1% for each turn of preparation after the first, up to 95% (so 8 turns gives 87%). Buildings and structures take weeks instead of turns. Camouflaged people and items go unnoticed unless they move or are touched; camouflaged buildings cannot be recognized from more than 50 feet away (adjust for the size and type of structure).
  • Mimicry: they can imitate the sound of any animal or monster almost perfectly, but not special attack forms.
  • Pickpockets: all are accomplished pickpockets, with a 70% chance of success.
  • Stronger members: for every 10 there is at least 1 with 2 hit dice; for every 30, 1 with 3 hit dice; for every 40, 1 with 4 hit dice. In the lair are a leader (AC 4, MV 12", HD 5, Dmg 1-12, +1 to hit) and 5 bodyguards (HD 4).
  • Weapons: usually clubs or swords, but 5% of any group carry blowguns with poison or paralyzing darts.

Habits: they usually live in areas of large mixed populations, lairing in ruins, deserted buildings, or other places humans once lived in or built. Their looks vary greatly, combining the worst features of each race. They speak broken Common mixed with animal cries and nonsense, and their names are almost always animal sounds.
system.hpNote: For every 10 at least 1 has 2 HD; every 30, 1 of 3 HD; every 40, 1 of 4 HD; bodyguards 4 HD (MMII p.92).

system.description:
The moon dog, also called the black hound or night prowler, is often mistaken for a harmful monster, but it actually protects mankind and hunts down evil predators in the night. It is almost never met in heavily populated areas. Usually only 1 is found, but in areas of great Evil there may be 2-8, and more on its home plane, Elysium (an Upper Outer Plane). Moon dogs serve only deities of Good and their great servants, such as devas, planetars, et al.

  • Armor class depends on light: AC 2 in bright, wholesome light; AC 0 in twilight; AC −2 in heavy shadow or darkness.
  • Bite: its normal attack, doing heavy damage.
  • Baying: all evil beings within 8" must save vs. spells or flee in panic (as a fear spell). Several moon dogs baying have a cumulative effect.
  • Howling: all creatures of Evil in a 4" radius take 5-8 points of damage per round. Each one not native to the Prime Material Plane also suffers great pain and has a cumulative 5% chance (per moon dog howling, per round) of being forced back to its own plane; magic resistance does not protect creatures of under 10 hit dice.
  • Spell-like powers (one at a time, 1 per round, at will, at 12th level): change self, dancing lights, darkness, improved invisibility, light, mirror image, non-detection, shades (once per day), and wall of fog.
  • Travel: it can become ethereal and travel astrally or ethereally.
  • Senses: double normal vision in all spectra, plus very keen hearing and smell, let it detect: evil; illusion (90%); invisibility, including the improved form, but only at 80%; magic (70%); and snares and pits (100%).
  • Hands: with grasping forepaws it sometimes uses small items.
  • Shadow pattern: in shadowy light it can move so as to create the effect of a hypnotic pattern of shadows, affecting only Evil creatures. At the same time, each creature of Good in the area gains protection from evil and remove fear. While weaving the pattern it cannot attack or do anything else.
  • Defenses: hit only by +2 or better weapons. Never surprised, and 50% likely to surprise opponents. Not subject to fear. It saves vs. cold, electricity, and fire/heat at +2, taking half or quarter damage accordingly.
  • Healing gifts: its whine acts as dispel illusion and its bark as dispel evil. Its lick gives cure disease, cure light wounds, or slow poison; each can help a given person only once per day. Spending 1 or more hours with a moon dog acts as dispel charm or remove curse.
  • Dispel magic: it can dispel magic, but this takes so much energy that it is forced back to its own plane at once.
  • Speech: its own language, speech with all canines and lupines, Common, and a limited telepathy. It talks with and helps humans and demi-humans of good will, but does not stay with them beyond the immediate need when evil threatens.

Description: dog-like, resembling a great wolfhound, but with a vaguely human head and grasping forepaws; it can easily walk on two legs (9" rate). Its coat is mottled dark gray with deepest black most common. Eye color is amber.
